_readme: Generated by scripts/research_map_db.py export-json. Do not hand-edit; it is an export of the same database the SQL commands query. Regenerate after changing the map, the schema, or the corpus.
relational_algebra: Make the research map queryable: a real relational database over what the project knows.
WHY THIS EXISTS. The research map is the index a session trusts to decide what is already known.
Prose you must read and remember is a weak guarantee; a query you run is a strong one. On 2026-07-30
one session re-derived work the repo already contained FOUR times, once at 1.52M tokens, because
nothing made "has this been settled?" a one-command question. This makes it one, and then goes
further: claims are JOINED to the evidence and the parameters they rest on, so an unsupported or
retracted claim is findable by query rather than by memory.
SOURCES. The database is assembled from five places, so no relation has to be maintained by hand
twice:
docs/research_map.md            settled, claim, hypothesis, supersedes, trap, derives
docs/findings/research_map_corpus.json  the SAME rows, untruncated -- see TEXT below
src/darwindiff/carroll6.py      parameter  (the registry is the single source of truth)
docs/findings/citation_audit.json   citation  (written by the citation-verification workflow)
docs/findings/*.md              document   (existence and supersession banners)
The document source matters: it lets a query ask "does this claim cite a file that exists, and does
that file carry a RETRACTED banner?" without anybody remembering to cross-check.
TEXT. The markdown is a READING view and `gen_research_map.cell()` cuts every cell in it -- settled
answers at 240 characters, claim statements at 230, traps at 220. This module parses that markdown,
so until 2026-08-04 the database held the CUT text and `settled` searched it: 87% of settled answers
were truncated, 35% of the corpus (83,957 of 242,118 characters) was unsearchable, and a miss
printed "This may be genuinely new work" -- a false negative indistinguishable from a true one, in
the tool built to prevent exactly that. `_rehydrate()` now widens every prose column back to the
corpus text after the parse. The markdown keeps its truncation; the database does not. Issue #228.
USAGE
python scripts/research_map_db.py settled daily      # <- RUN THIS BEFORE STARTING WORK
python scripts/research_map_db.py check              # integrity constraints, exit 1 on violation
python scripts/research_map_db.py trace D1           # what a claim rests on, and what rests on it
python scripts/research_map_db.py param scav_rat     # everything known about one parameter
python scripts/research_map_db.py superseded 0.408   # is this number dead?
python scripts/research_map_db.py dangerous          # live claims resting on weak ground
python scripts/research_map_db.py sql "SELECT ..."   # arbitrary read-only SQL
ENFORCED (`check` exits 1). Relational algebra, written in SQL in CONSTRAINTS below:
pi_cl(sigma_{live}(CLAIM)) INTERSECT pi_old(SUPERSEDES)   = {}   on normalised PROSE, not ids
sigma_{mode=inductive AND numbers IS NULL}(CLAIM)         = {}   presence only, see caveat
sigma_{doc NOT IN DOCUMENT}(CLAIM)                        = {}   DOCUMENT is the REPO, not disk
sigma_{verdict=RESOLVES_MISMATCH}(CITATION)               = {}
sigma_{verdict IN (DEAD, FABRICATED)}(CITATION)           = {}
sigma_{doc IS NULL}(SETTLED)                              = {}
sigma_{status IS NULL}(CLAIM)                             = {}
sigma_{prose ENDS WITH ellipsis}(SETTLED u CLAIM u ...)   = {}   no markdown cut leaked in
REPORTED BUT NOT ENFORCED (`check` prints, never fails). These are real properties that currently
have violations; gating on them would fail every run and train readers to ignore the gate:
sigma_{live}(CLAIM) |><| sigma_{local_only}(DOCUMENT), sole cite       -- 2 rows
CLAIM |><| SUPPORTS |><| sigma_{gate != exit0}(EVIDENCE) where live     -- 39 rows
sigma_{live}(CLAIM) |><| sigma_{retracted}(DOCUMENT)                    -- 26 rows
CLAIM - pi_cl(SUPPORTS)                                                 -- 291 rows
THREE CAVEATS, stated because a passing `check` otherwise reads stronger than it is:
* "carries its untrained null" is a PRESENCE check on the merged `n / null` column. The corpus
has no separate null field, so no constraint here can verify a matched baseline exists.
* the citation constraints run over the audit's EXCEPTION rows only (1 of 130). `check` prints
its own coverage line for this reason.
* DOCUMENT is built from `git ls-files` plus the declared LOCAL_ONLY_DOCS, never from a disk
walk. Enumerating from disk made the orphan constraint pass on the author's machine and fail
in CI, where the seven gitignored notes do not exist. The mirror is now byte-identical from a
tracked-files-only checkout, which is the negative control ADR-0004 asks for.

citation.ddl:
CREATE TABLE citation (
    doi        TEXT,
    verdict    TEXT,                 -- RESOLVES_MATCHES | RESOLVES_MISMATCH | DEAD | SUSPECT_FABRICATED
    claimed    TEXT,
    actual     TEXT,
    doc        TEXT,
    deliberate INTEGER DEFAULT 0     -- 1 = cites a known-bad DOI on purpose, to record that it is bad
)

rows.claimed: Parekh et al. 2006 iron-cycle model underlying Darwin's routines
rows.actual: Parekh 2006 Physical and biological regulation of the soft tissue carbon pump

claim.ddl:
CREATE TABLE claim (
    cl_id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    statement     TEXT,
    mode          TEXT,             -- deductive | inductive | abductive
    status        TEXT,             -- live | retracted | superseded | pending | unverified
    detail        TEXT,             -- derivation, or what prompted it, or the evidence summary
    n             TEXT,
    null_baseline TEXT,
    doc           TEXT,
    parameter     TEXT,             -- FK-ish into parameter.name when the claim is about one
    track         TEXT              -- track1 | track2 | method | data
)

rows.statement: A prognostic-only operator with zero forcing inputs losing to seasonal AR(1) is close to a foregone conclusion, because AR(1) implicitly encodes the seasonal forcing cycle the emulator cannot see.
rows.detail: Abduction to the best explanation of the null, grounded in a verified structural difference from every comparator. It is the strongest ALTERNATIVE explanation and must be closed by a forcing-channel ablation before the deflation is publishable as a ceiling claim.
rows.null_baseline: the multiseed flag list contains no --forcing; scripts/emulator_poc.py:1211 gates forcing on `_use_forc = bool(forcings) and 'forcing' in z.files and z['forcing'].ndim == 4`, with --forcing declared but unused at :131 ('Empty = pure prognostic'). Comparators all take forcing: Samudra tauuo/tauvo/hfds; Skakala 2026 PAR, wind, precipitation, surface heat flux, SST, SSS, MLD; Smith 2026 T, S, SSH, wind speed, MLD, three velocity components, shortwave, PAR, cyclic day-of-year; Martinez Balbontin MLD, SSH, SST, SSS. Our own repo already says it (2026-07-23_emulator_baseline_matrix.md:90: 'The fix is an input, not a bigger network').

rows.statement: alpfe's recovery profile is flat and one-sided (initialization-anchored) - the EXPECTED signature of a well-specified homogeneous forcing property. Claim 'consistent with a homogeneous forcing scalar', not 'sharply data-identified'.
rows.detail: An explanatory reading of a flat profile that would otherwise be read as failure; the honesty caveat is attached because the diagnostic cannot yet separate the two readings.
rows.null_baseline: profile-likelihood span 0.0235 (the 2026-07-19 diagnostic, reported in the 2026-07-20 architecture note) while alpfe recovers 9-10/10

rows.statement: Both reproducibility failures found are the same shape: the config a run DECLARES is not checked against the config it RAN.
rows.detail: A unifying explanation abstracted from two independent surprises; it motivated the gate fix, which is the test.
rows.null_baseline: Failure 1: published recipe missing three levers. Failure 2: DANIELS_RPICPOC_W=1 declared with the PANGAEA file unstaged - anchor skipped with a [warn], run trained anyway, verify_run.py passed at exit 0 with R_PICPOC at 0.20-0.26x Carroll.

rows.statement: Composition does NOT carry the basin PIC:POC spread; per-calcifier calcification EFFICIENCY does, and it varies with environment / carbonate chemistry. This adjudicates the two competing statements ('depends on composition' vs 'depends on environmental condition and carbonate chemistry') in favour of environment.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of a surprise (flat calcifier fraction under a 113x bulk spread). Its corroboration - that USE_ENV_RAIN_RATIO reproduced the spread while cocco-only gating did not - is RETRODICTION, not a tested novel prediction; the measured refutation half is what carries the row.
rows.null_baseline: calcifier fraction 1.4x spread (0.153/0.134/0.109); bulk PIC:POC 113x (0.034/0.729/0.006); implied per-calcifier R 92x (0.22/5.4/0.06); Chl2-PIC correlation r=0.50 eqpac, r=0.73 SO

rows.statement: Darwin's two uncertain closures are non-identifiable for DISTINCT reasons, and that taxonomy - not a recovery count - is the honest Track-2 science.
rows.detail: An explanatory taxonomy proposed to reconcile two apparently similar failures. It predicted something it was not built to explain - that a scavenging closure fit to held-out DFe would appear to 'work' while returning an equifinal, meaningless scav_rat - and the 32x flat-profile sweep tested exactly that prediction.
rows.null_baseline: calcite R_PICPOC: observable ~ the parameter, obs too sparse/noisy => DATA-LIMITED (null, Maranon-consistent). iron scav_rat: observable densely env-predictable (GLOBAL p 0.000 on ~1214 cells) but a low-information projection of the rate => OBSERVABILITY-LIMITED, structural, NOT data-limited.

rows.statement: diatomgraz's recovery counts largely track where the prior sits rather than what the network learned.
rows.detail: Proposed to explain why diatomgraz counts were high and unstable; confirmed by a control the explanation was not built from (the architecture-matched untrained run).
rows.null_baseline: diatomgraz scores 0.640 untrained at n=50 (job 227777). The 35/50 'non-circular handle' result is P = 0.447 against an architecture-matched untrained baseline of 34/50 (MLD_CHANNEL=1, job 227876) - it beats an untrained network by ONE seed. The obs-only 11/50 is BELOW chance (lower-tail P = 1.6e-09).

rows.statement: FeT is the only emulator tracer that beats no baseline, and the signature (real tendency structure, zero skill against any reference) is what missing forcing looks like.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of a surprise (directional information present but uncashable); the predicted fix - dust/PAR input channels - has NOT been tested, so it is not yet a result.
rows.null_baseline: FeT: persistence -0.805, damped -0.869, seasonal clim -0.329, anomaly-persistence -1.054, anomR2(clim) -0.138, corr_tend +0.367. Negative at every depth (k0 -0.69 to k4 -1.04) and in both eqpac sub-bands (eq -0.88, north -0.54).

rows.statement: Identifiability tracks the observational constraint: sparse/indirect iron observations give sloppy profiles, a direct ratio observation gives a curved one.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of the iron-vs-calcite contrast; corroborated externally by Tagliabue 2016 but not itself derived or independently predicted here.
rows.null_baseline: R_PICPOC rel_span 46.6 with the Daniels/RATIO_W anchor vs alpfe 0.207 / scav_rat 0.196 without a comparable direct anchor.

rows.statement: Information theory and experiment contradict each other for eqpac iron, and the coherent reading is forward-model misspecification rather than an information limit.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of a surprise (adding the information the Fisher score names makes recovery worse), unifying four independent lines. It makes an untested prediction about TPOSE iron, so it is not yet a result.
rows.null_baseline: Fisher: dfe_sub 6426x, cond 12545 -> 2.1, align 0.98. But GEOTRACES bins in-AOI already surface=26, subsurface=28, and GEOTRACES_SUB_W 1->3->8 degrades scav_rat 9/10 -> 5/10 -> 1/10. tan phi: eqpac FeT residual >= ||data||, phi = 90 degrees.

rows.statement: Neural-BGC's success is a data-density result, and the same method pointed at DarwinDiff's tracers would fail on observation counts alone.
rows.detail: Best explanation of why a nearly identical architecture succeeds there and fails here; its prediction (observation-densification gives a flat or negative result) is PARKED, untested.
rows.null_baseline: Neural-BGC trained on ~16.7M DO + 6.2M NO3 WOD in-situ samples (1965-2024); Arabian Sea DO RMSE 13.78 (NN) vs 15.70 (NPZD), Canary 6.96 vs 9.29. Our targets: ~14 GEOTRACES iron surface cells; R_PICPOC on a single Daniels anchor, whose removal collapses R_PICPOC 50/50 → 6/50 epoch-matched at 2000 epochs (4/50 at 1500).

rows.statement: Raw parameter sensitivity is not identifiability: diatomgraz is by far the stiffest box parameter yet is the data-blocked one.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of a surprise (stiffest parameter is also the blocked one). It is why the Fisher — which folds in the observation footprint — not the raw Jacobian is the right object. NOT yet tested against a prediction it was not built to explain, so not yet a result.
rows.null_baseline: |S| ranking: diatomgraz->diatom -7.110, R_PICPOC->PIC +1.000, alpfe->DFe_surf +0.607, scav_rat->DFe_surf -0.490. Proposed explanation: the bSi/biomass observable routes through the model's OWN diatom biomass, which compensates, so a large d(biomass)/d(param) does not translate into an identifiable observable.

rows.statement: scav_rat is identifiable from the VERTICAL STRUCTURE of dissolved iron, not from its surface concentration; and the two observation levels identify different parameters.
rows.detail: This is the strong form of abduction: 2026-07-22_column_osse_result.md proposed the mechanism (alpfe sets profile AMPLITUDE, scav_rat sets SHAPE) from a synthetic 1-D column, it was pre-registered as a decision rule nine days before the run, and it was then confirmed on real GEOTRACES data on a different code path.
rows.null_baseline: so_sub 33/50 (P(>=k)=1.70e-28) vs so_surf 14/50 (not above chance), volume-matched 14 vs 13 bins, Fisher exact two-sided P = 0.000268. The inversion: so_surf alpfe 49/50 / scav_rat 14/50; so_sub alpfe 14/50 / scav_rat 33/50. Controls: verify_run exit 0 on all four arms, GATE_FAIL=0; prior_so_abl bitwise identical to prior_so_only (0.000e+00 over 50 shared seeds); so_repro bitwise identical to parent 238079 (but only 10/50 seeds, a TIMEOUT, and no count from it is quoted).

rows.statement: scav_rat was leaning on the Darwin-pattern terms, not on the real iron data.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of scav_rat's clean 26/50 -> 0/50 collapse when only the Darwin-derived loss terms were removed, while alpfe and R_PICPOC survived on the same real anchors. NOTE: no prediction it was not built to explain has yet been tested - the doc asserts it in passing as 'a diagnosable reason'.

rows.statement: scav_rat's poor RECOVERY is an optimization/coverage limit, not a hard information degeneracy.
rows.detail: Best explanation of the gap between well-conditioned information and poor recovery; it is a reading of two measurements, not itself measured.
rows.null_baseline: iron-pair condition 2.2 with the real surf+sub data, versus scav_rat per-AOI 25/50 in the flagship

rows.statement: The '1.7% parameter contribution' hook is misleading unqualified, and the surviving hook is stronger: whether a biogeochemical parameter appears identifiable depends on how the cost function is WEIGHTED ACROSS DEPTH.
rows.detail: Reinterprets a surprising number by locating its cause (depth weighting) and connects to an independent published statement it was not built to explain - Carroll naming iron scavenging as an upper-ocean leader.

rows.statement: The alpfe and diatomgraz profiles are ONE-SIDED by construction, which is the mechanism for the standing 'alpfe reads FLAT yet recovers 9-10/10' contradiction.
rows.detail: The one-sidedness itself is deductive from PARAM_BOUNDS and the target values; the claim that it EXPLAINS the long-standing FLAT-yet-recovers puzzle is an abduction, and it also predicts that 'diatomgraz FLAT -> structural non-identifiability' is measured on a grid where 94% of the log-range lies below the true value.

The other four are far less truncated: scav_rat 0.65, Smallgrow 0.63, Biggrow 0.49, R_PICPOC 0.37. The bracketing guard only fires when the profile MINIMUM lands on an endpoint index, so it does not catch this.

rows.statement: The alpfe<->scav_rat degeneracy is breakable ONLY by a new observable that projects source and sink differently; no estimator or architecture change ever will, and every genuinely degeneracy-breaking observable requires a model extension because the 0-D box homogenizes away the vertical/section structure that carries the information.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of why every estimator fails identically. Its prediction - that a 1-D column adds a second non-null Fisher eigenvalue - was subsequently TESTED and confirmed (2026-07-22_column_osse_result.md), which upgrades this from a proposal to a supported abduction.
rows.null_baseline: confirmed across 5 estimators + EKI; 8 ranked candidate observables; top pick #3 = 1-D vertical column fit to 50-level FeT + full-depth GEOTRACES

rows.statement: The analytic two-anchor OSSE's predicted degeneracy geometry transfers to the full differentiable box.
rows.detail: The analytic OSSE predicted |rho| 1 -> 0.20 for the dust-source anchor BEFORE the real-box run (the real-box script is explicitly the promotion of the analytic one); the real box independently returned 0.195.
rows.null_baseline: analytic OSSE |rho| 1 -> 0.20; real box dust-source config |rho| = 0.195.

rows.statement: The binding constraint on UDE closure identifiability is state-space coverage - which states the forcing visits - not the optimizer, the regularizer, or the integrator.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of the surprise (152,000x loss reduction yet 288% off-trajectory error). The EXP-D regularization sweep is what tests it, and it comes out invariant (2.877 in all four configs) exactly as the explanation requires. NOTE: the doc does not state that the coverage hypothesis was formed before EXP-D - both ran in job 8524801 - so read this as an explanation with a confirming test, not a pre-registered prediction. It is the same lesson as Track-1 arriving in the forward-UDE setting.
rows.null_baseline: visited 0.65% vs full-range 288%; regularization sweep invariant at 2.877. Motivates the #176 profile-targeting forcing design (scripts/ude_forcing_design.py).

rows.statement: The box's iron scavenging is a triple simplification of Darwin3/Parekh, and what the box drops is exactly what is spatially variable - the surrogate-gap fingerprint behind scav_rat's per-cell requirement.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of why scav_rat specifically needed per-cell treatment in Paper 1, grounded in a line-by-line comparison of the box term against the upstream formulation.
rows.null_baseline: The box sink scav_rat_per_day*DFe*POC (carroll6.py:221,282; transport.py:85) scavenges TOTAL dissolved Fe (not free Fe'), uses LINEAR POC weighting where Darwin uses POC^0.58, and has NO ligand chemistry. Proposed replacement anchors at eps=0, p=1, r0=0.0521 to be byte-identical.

rows.statement: The carbonate closure check passes but is UNINFORMATIVE - it cannot distinguish 'learned the chemistry' from 'copied the input', because DIC and ALK are nearly persistent at monthly cadence.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of an implausibly good agreement, and it made a prediction it was not built to explain - that the same low tendency-to-variance ratio should make DIC/ALK score POORLY against persistence - which the per-tracer split then confirmed.
rows.null_baseline: pCO2 380.33 (v05) vs 380.84 uatm (emulator), 0.51 uatm apart; Revelle ~10 implies a DIC error of roughly 0.05% over one step. Confirmed prediction: 3-D per-tracer skill vs persistence DIC 0.376 / ALK 0.305, the two LOWEST of six tracers.

rows.statement: The column OSSE's amplitude/shape mechanism, proposed on synthetic data, is confirmed on real GEOTRACES observations nine days later
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of a self-twin surprise, which then predicted something it was not built to explain and was tested on real data.
rows.null_baseline: 2026-07-22_column_osse_result.md: alpfe sets profile AMPLITUDE, scav_rat sets its SHAPE (e-folding ~sqrt(kz/scav)); moved CRLB(log scav) from 4.2e6 in a 0-D box to 0.005 in a column. CAVEAT: 4.2e6 is the RIDGE FLOOR (labelled 'rank-1 null - unidentified (ridge, as documented)'), so read it as 'unconstrained', never as a 10^6-fold ratio (standing rule, docs/findings/2026-07-29_math_audit_index.md §3). A surface concentration is an amplitude, a profile is a shape - so it predicted the exact surface/subsurface inversion measured on 2026-07-31, from a different code path.

rows.statement: The controlled Somes 2021 experiment lands on the degeneracy prediction: varying the iron source ~5x and retuning scavenging to hold concentration gives tau x4.8.
rows.detail: The single-box steady-state degeneracy argument predicted the residence-time response; an independent published controlled experiment, not designed to test our framing, matched it.

rows.statement: The covariate lever is orthogonal to network capacity: NN size and patch-overlap both failed to move these parameters because they change capacity, while covariates change input information.
rows.detail: An explanation proposed post-hoc for why two prior levers returned ~0 and this one did not. It is stated in the doc as interpretation, NOT as a pre-registered prediction that was then tested, so it stays below result-grade.

rows.detail: A reinterpretation offered as the best account of what the emulator work was producing; it has not yet made a tested prediction.

rows.statement: The design-then-vet-then-validate pipeline's most valuable output was not a recovery number but the finding that the project's remaining gaps are mostly identifiability LIMITS, not to-dos.
rows.detail: An inference to the best explanation of why most enumerated improvements were foregone or structurally pre-determined; the kills are code-grounded rather than assumed.

rows.statement: The earlier 'θ* is a saddle' result was under-convergence from a single start, not a genuine rank-deficiency.
rows.detail: Proposed as the explanation of a surprise and then tested — the multi-start is the test, and it removed the negative eigenvalue while leaving the sloppy ridge.

rows.detail: Proposed as the best explanation of a uniform negative, then tested by a diagnostic that could have falsified it (concentrated error would have meant a discretization artifact).

rows.statement: The four observables are jointly IDENTIFIABLE (full-rank information) but RECOVERABILITY is design-fragile - and the 3-of-4 frontier is structural, not an optimization limit.
rows.detail: Abduction to explain the surprise that MLD rescues diatomgraz in the anchors-only loss (10/10) but not once the Darwin-pattern terms are present (0/10). It made a prediction it was not built to explain - that the failure persists at doubled epochs - and that prediction was tested and held.

rows.statement: The growth pair is neither signal-deleted by z-scoring nor mutually degenerate; it is information-starved, and Biggrow's signal is concentrated in Chl2 while Smallgrow's is diffuse and routed through iron.
rows.detail: The starvation explanation replaced two refuted hypotheses and produced a discriminating prediction it was not built to explain (Smallgrow should NOT respond to a Chl2 up-weight), which was then confirmed twice at n=20 and n=50.
rows.null_baseline: z/raw response: Biggrow 0.949, Smallgrow 0.610, diatomgraz 0.332 (most damaged, yet recovers). Smallgrow+Biggrow 2x2 cond 1.20, least degenerate of all 15 pairs, conditional correlation -0.088. Relative Fisher: diatomgraz 1.000, alpfe 0.140, R_PICPOC 0.099, Biggrow 0.055, Smallgrow 0.053, scav_rat 0.026. Per-field: Biggrow Chl2 25.9 vs ~2.5-3.1 elsewhere; Smallgrow FeT 14.4 > its own Chl5 9.3. Scope caveat: synthetic self-twin, 240-cell synthetic AOI.

rows.statement: The honest fix for the sloppy ridge is Fisher-eigenbasis reparameterization plus a prior on the sloppy direction (Lever-1), not longer optimization.
rows.detail: Best explanation of what did and did not change under a harder optimizer; the prescription has not been graded against a recovery count here.
rows.null_baseline: Converging harder removed the spurious negative eigenvalue but the ~2.69-decade sloppy ridge remains. Implementation: scripts/analysis/eki_core.py::reparam_with_prior.

rows.statement: The iron source↔scavenging degeneracy DarwinDiff recovers is the FeMIP problem, and the field does not appear to have named it as a formal identifiability problem.
rows.detail: Inference to the best explanation of the FeMIP spread, and it made a prediction (Somes' controlled experiment) it was not built to explain, which landed.
rows.null_baseline: Tagliabue 2016 Table 2 (13 models): residence time 3.7 → 626 yr (169×), mean concentration 0.58 ± 0.14 nM (~24%), total input flux ~140× (sediment 0-194 Gmol/yr). τ = inventory/input reproduces every model's τ exactly; 169× = 130× input × 1.3× inventory. Somes 2021: vary combined atmospheric+sedimentary source ~5×, retune scavenging to hold concentration → τ ×4.8 (predicted). rows.statement: Forming J^T J squares the condition number, and with n <= 6 there is no cost argument for ever doing it in this codebase.
rows.detail: the eigenvalue map lambda = sigma^2 is algebra, not a metaphor
rows.null_baseline: J~^T J~ = V Sigma_s^2 V^T so lambda_i = sigma_i^2 and kappa(J~^T J~) = kappa(J~)^2. Digits: normal-equations path loses 2*log10(kappa), QR/SVD path loses log10(kappa). float32 carries ~7.22 decimal digits, float64 ~15.95; at kappa = 2930 in float32 that is 0.29 vs 3.6 surviving digits. J~ is at most m x 6 so a full SVD is free. Applies to the DIAGNOSTICS (identifiability_sloppiness.py, observation_design.py), not the training loop (first-order Adam never forms J^T J)

rows.statement: Residual magnitude grows with Delta-t, so long-gap pairs carry much larger targets and dominate an MSE training loss; mixed training is therefore effectively long-gap training and the one-month pairs contribute little gradient. If so, a 1/Delta-t loss weighting recovers most of the uniform-Delta-t benefit without rebuilding the cube.
rows.predicts: Reweighting the existing mixed-Delta-t training set by 1/Delta-t should lift mixed-train skill on the uniform validation subset from +0.0026 toward +0.4756, at no data cost.
rows.falsifier: 1/Delta-t weighting leaves uniform-val skill near +0.0026, in which case the gap is not a loss-weighting artifact and the cube rebuild for uniformity is required.

rows.statement: Observations-only can carry the paper's headline if the strict arm (obs-only targets AND literature IC) clears 3-of-4 against architecture-matched baselines.

rows.falsifier: 2-of-4 keeps the flagship and makes obs-only the strongest robustness section, which is not a demotion. Accepted cost either way: the joint trio goes 25/50 -> 0/50. Written with zero JSONs on disk; do not reinterpret against it.

rows.statement: Under Darwin's fixed ligand, delta-56Fe recreates the lumped-removal degeneracy rather than breaking it.
rows.predicts: The fixed ligand freezes the scavenging-versus-colloidal-pumping split that carries the sink isotope signal (Koenig & Tagliabue 2021), and uptake plus scavenging fractionate dissolved delta-56Fe in the SAME direction. Its real strength is source apportionment, which the dust anchor already does out-of-manifold.
rows.falsifier: A cheap fixed-vs-dynamic-ligand OSSE as a decision gate before any port. Expectation is NO-GO; confirm before spending on a tracer doubling plus 6-7 new knobs. Hold as a v2 bet.

rows.statement: The surrogate Fisher eigenstructure transfers to ECCO-Darwin, so the sloppy/stiff directions and the EKI reparameterization are GCM claims and not merely surrogate-conditional ones.
rows.predicts: The GCM's cross-parameter sensitivity ranking by sensitivity-to-own-observable matches the surrogate's: diatomgraz ≫ R_PICPOC > alpfe > scav_rat, measured from the 17-deck OAT ensemble at the same two FD steps (s = 1.1, 1.2).
rows.falsifier: A different GCM ranking. Signs are NOT the test (they agree by construction because the box reuses Darwin's own source/sink forms), and no single magnitude is the test either.

rows.statement: An 8-run one-at-a-time ECCO-Darwin v05 perturbation ensemble about the Carroll optimum would validate (or refute) transferring the surrogate Fisher eigenstructure to the GCM.
rows.predicts: Two v05 forward runs at +/-10-20% per observable parameter (namelist edits: data.darwin for alpfe/scav_rat; data.traits PALAT / a_R_PICPOC for diatomgraz/R_PICPOC — traits-override-safe), plus the existing control. Form d ln<tracer>/d ln(param) by central difference on bin_average'd AOI footprints. Sign agreement (a) is expected to PASS by construction; magnitude ratio (b) is informative; the LOAD-BEARING test is (c) whether the four-parameter RANKING by sensitivity to its own observable matches the surrogate's diatomgraz >> R_PICPOC > alpfe > scav_rat.
rows.falsifier: A different cross-parameter ranking in Darwin — which would mean the sloppy direction differs and the paper's sloppy/stiff decomposition and EKI reparameterization do not transfer. Blocked on GCM access / Jon's compute; out of scope for this repo's box. Surrogate side now has a committed tool (scripts/analysis/surrogate_jacobian_obsop.py) but its run is data-blocked on AICR.

rows.statement: v05 GCM perturbation runs will validate the surrogate Fisher eigenstructure only if the cross-parameter sensitivity RANKING agrees; the ensemble is otherwise uninformative because signs agree by construction.
rows.predicts: The 17-run OAT ensemble, pushed through the same observation operators as the inverse problem, should reproduce diatomgraz >> R_PICPOC > alpfe > scav_rat.
rows.falsifier: A different ranking in the GCM would block transferring the surrogate Fisher eigenbasis (sloppy/stiff directions, the EKI reparameterization) to ECCO-Darwin. Also requires a demonstrated convergence-with-integration-length, since short runs measure transient rather than equilibrated sensitivity.

rows.predicts: A profile-likelihood on diatomgraz with the MLD channel ON will show curvature, where the SST-only profile was FLAT.
rows.falsifier: A flat profile with MLD on would mean the 10/10 is band-edge luck rather than identifiability. Explicit instruction: do NOT re-headline diatomgraz as 'identifiable' until this runs. Still open as of STATUS.md - the multi-start identifiability array (#152) is what confirms it.

rows.statement: Gauge-fix the scavenging closure by construction (remove log_r0, mean-centre log G over a fixed reference support so scav_rat carries the entire geometric-mean level and theta carries only shape), then ask whether real iron data resolves any SHAPE at all
rows.predicts: Pre-registered answer: NO. At initialization the readout is zero and p=1 so G=1 bitwise, reproducing the current bilinear sink to round-off - the cleanest untrained null in the project.
rows.falsifier: A gauge-fixed closure whose learned shape clears its own untrained null on real Southern Ocean iron

rows.statement: The forward-emulator rollout ceiling is not irreducible: a flat 2-D FFT on a curved, land-masked grid produces a state-dependent, boundary-concentrated error that the constant-bias test could not have detected.
rows.predicts: A geometry-aware operator should beat the flat FFT on a rebuilt global cube - the clean experiment is scoped.
rows.falsifier: A geometry-aware operator that does not beat the flat FFT. Blocked so far: jobs 8512977/8512998 were inconclusive because the AOI cubes are non-geographic (empty interior) and cannot resolve coastal versus interior, and the global cube is off disk.

rows.statement: The pooled eqpac+natl / smaller-regularized-closure E2 calcite rerun will NOT recover identifiability, because the binding constraint is Omega support rather than sample size or closure capacity.
rows.predicts: Pooling two basins reaches only 0.25 dex, still below the 0.30-dex threshold; a smaller closure cannot manufacture an Omega-dependence the data does not contain. Therefore the rerun returns NON-IDENTIFIABLE again and the terminal result is the identifiability-limits write-up.
rows.falsifier: A pooled or smaller-closure rerun returning IDENTIFIABLE with a stable, significant exponent. NOTE: the 2026-07-29 pooling finding makes the pooled arm actively misleading — a pooled 'pass' would be a between-basin contrast, so the falsifier must be a PER-AOI pass.

rows.statement: The scav_rat and alpfe profile likelihoods are slow because they are the sloppy iron directions.
rows.predicts: The flat-direction re-optimization inside each profile grid point should be what stalls, which is why the single-evaluation GN-Fisher is the practical substitute.
rows.falsifier: A slow node or the refine loop could equally explain the >1:45 h cancellations; the OBSERVATION (these two are ~5x slower than R_PICPOC/diatomgraz at 23 min) is confirmed, the MECHANISM is a plausible inference, not proven.

rows.statement: The Daniels calcite anchor constrains the PRODUCT R_PICPOC * f_calc, where f_calc is the share of production done by calcifying types — so a box that applies the ratio to more types than Darwin compensates by inflating R_PICPOC.
rows.predicts: R_PICPOC inflation should be spatially ordered by local community composition, larger where the calcifying fraction is smaller. Sign and ordering are confirmed in the two anchored basins, and the measured offsets are order 1-2 rather than the ~24x a whole-model structural mismatch implies; the quantitative 1/f law is refuted under the correct Chl2+Chl3 grouping.

rows.question: What is the precise honest label for the growth pair {Smallgrow, Biggrow}?
rows.answer: 'Unobservable by construction' is the honest ACCOUNTING call, but the precise label is PRACTICAL NON-IDENTIFIABILITY UNDER THE CURRENT DESIGN (23-yr climatology, no group-resolved production observable). It is not an absolute law.

rows.question: What metrics should a UDE closure-recovery result report?
rows.answer: (1) On-support density-weighted closure error - the headline; (2) off-support extrapolation error, reported separately and explicitly labeled; (3) posterior/ensemble width as a function of DFe (deep-ensemble std + Laplace predictive std) overlaid on the visitation histogram - this IS the identifiability map; (4) the DFe-coverage plot per arm; (5) held-out-CONDITION closure error (leave-one-regime-out; equifinality is invisible to within-trajectory time splits); (6) trajectory MSE ONLY to demonstrate the decoupling, never as the success criterion.

rows.question: Which forward model should the Carroll-6 calibration loss be backpropped through - parameter-conditioned FNO (A), mechanistic UDE (B), or SBI?
rows.answer: (B), the mechanistic UDE. transport.py::column_tendency (L121) is ALREADY f(Carroll-6, forcing) -> dstate, autograd-clean and mass-conserving by construction, and needs zero new GCM runs. (A) is data-blocked: it requires a perturbed-parameter ensemble spanning the Carroll-6 box and DarwinDiff has exactly one v05 run (~5 TB/run vs 1.43 TB free). SBI shares (A)'s PPE cost and its robustness fix (RoPE/FRISBI) needs ground-truth parameter labels we structurally cannot supply.

rows.question: What is the flagship emulator's skill on genuine one-month transitions?
rows.answer: +0.0026 vs persistence (one seed negative), on the n=21 uniform-dt validation subset. A uniform-dt-trained model with the same pair count scores +0.4756 on that identical subset (delta +0.4730). The flagship is a ~2-month operator: median training gap ~61 days.

rows.question: How biased is ECCO-Darwin v05 surface chlorophyll against MODIS-Aqua in the subpolar N. Atlantic?
rows.answer: -0.696 dex = 0.20x, i.e. ~5x LOW, over 176 months (2003-01 to 2018-11), RMSE 0.912 dex. MODIS retrieval noise floor is 0.130 dex, so the bias exceeds it by 5x. Survives coverage filtering (>=90% coverage, n=125 -> -0.601).

rows.question: How much storage do we actually have on Explorer, and where should TB-scale inputs be staged?
rows.answer: /projects/schultz is 36 TB total with 8.2 TB free — NOT '3.3 PB'. Stage on /scratch (1.9 PB, 810 TB free, VAST). 'Home 111 TB free' is the shared /home filesystem (255 TB VAST), not a personal quota.

rows.question: Where is the ECCO-Darwin v05 monthly training data and how big is it?
rows.answer: /projects/schultz/qi.zim/ecco_darwin_v5/output/monthly on Explorer: 280 monthly timesteps, 16 fields (ALK, apCO2, Chl1-5, CO2_flux, DIC, FeT, mldDepth, PIC, POC, POSi, SST, wspeed), native LLC270, ~50 levels, ~190 MB/field/step, ~850 GB total, ~23 years. NO velocity fields in this tree - the emulator learns dynamics implicitly from the tracer time series plus surface forcing; it does not need prescribed transport the way the UDE E2 did.

rows.question: What is the observed PIC:POC across the three AOIs, and can one scalar rain ratio match it?
rows.answer: 0.0065 in southernoceanpac, 0.0308 in eqpac, 0.722 in natlsubpolar — a ~111x spread — against Carroll's single published R_PICPOC = 0.04245. The doc calls this a stronger statement about the identifiability of a scalar rain ratio than anything in the bias analysis, and it is measured rather than inferred.

rows.question: What is the observed PIC:POC spread across the three AOIs versus the single published rain ratio?
rows.answer: 0.0065, 0.031 and 0.72 across the three regions - about a hundred times (elsewhere quoted 111x) spread against a single published value of 0.042. Critically this is a STANDING-STOCK ratio from the target caches; Daniels is a PRODUCTION ratio. The distinction must be made explicitly, not glossed.

rows.question: Which R_PICPOC value does ECCO-Darwin v05 actually integrate — the published 0.04245 or something else?
rows.answer: 0.041886, applied to plankton types 2 and 3 only, set in `data.traits:36` as `0.0, 2*4.1886E-2, 4*0.0`. The 0.04245 in `data.darwin:53` is not merely overridden, it is UNREACHABLE under v05's compile flags. Gap to published = 1.35%, far inside the Excellent band, so no recovery verdict changes — but the manuscript must say which it grades against. Runtime handle: every v05 run writes `darwin_traits.txt` after the namelist read and the hasPIC gate.

rows.question: Which of the three R_PICPOC values in the v05 config actually runs?
rows.answer: 0.0418860 from data.traits:92 (plankton types 2 and 3, the calcifiers; the other five carry 0.0). The 0.04245 in data.darwin's DARWIN_RANDOM_PARAMS is INERT because DARWIN_READ_TRAITS runs last (darwin_init_fixed.F:382) and overwrites the generated array. Editing val_R_PICPOC changes nothing. alpfe and scav_rat ARE safe to edit in data.darwin. Carroll's published 0.04245 differs from the running 0.0418860 by 1.35%.

rows.question: Which of the three R_PICPOC values in the v05 llc270 deck is the one the model actually integrates?
rows.answer: 0.0418860, from data.traits &DARWIN_TRAITS entries 2 and 3 (the calcifiers); the other five types carry 0.0. The array reads R_PICPOC = 0.0, 2*4.188600000000000E-002, 4*0.0. data.darwin:53 val_R_PICPOC = 0.04245 under &DARWIN_RANDOM_PARAMS is INERT. Precedence in pkg/darwin/darwin_init_fixed.F: DARWIN_GENERATE_RANDOM at line 357 fills the array, then DARWIN_READ_TRAITS runs LAST at line 382 and overwrites it. Carroll's published 0.04245 vs v05's running 0.0418860 is a 1.35% difference - inside the 5% Excellent band, changes no verdict. Caveat: no observed STDOUT.0000 namelist echo yet. NOTE (later doc): docs/findings/2026-07-30_rain_ratio_which_value_is_live.md gives the traits array at data.traits:36 (not :92), upgrades 'inert' to 'UNREACHABLE under v05 compile flags', and corrects the framing - &DARWIN_RANDOM_PARAMS and &DARWIN_TRAIT_PARAMS are BOTH read from data.darwin.

rows.question: How many real observation cells actually exist, per AOI and per parameter?
rows.answer: 112 of 2851 ocean cells carry any real information - 3.9%. Per AOI (ocean cells / iron surf/sub / Daniels / POSi / union): eqpac 1071 / 26/28 / 34 / 7 / 59; natlsubpolar 484 / 13/13 / 26 / 4 / 39; southernoceanpac 1296 / 13/14 / 0 / 0 / 14. Per parameter: alpfe 55 (1.9%), scav_rat 55 (1.9%), R_PICPOC 60 (2.1%, 2 of 3 AOIs), diatomgraz 11 (0.4%, 2 of 3 AOIs), Smallgrow/Biggrow 0. The zeros are exact, not small - southernoceanpac has NO Daniels and NO POSi cells. With the Darwin block off, 96.1% of cells have identically zero loss gradient.

rows.question: What is v05 daily's true time span and the MODIS overlap?
rows.answer: 1992-01-03 to 2018-12-31 (the old '2012-03-31' was a delta_t artifact). MODIS-Aqua overlap nearly doubles, 9.2 -> 16 years. 'Use MODIS, not PACE' still holds (PACE launched 2024).

rows.question: How many parameters does the BINN paper actually learn, and what are the 'six processes'?
rows.answer: 21 scalar parameters per location - the final layer has 21 output neurons, one per biogeochemical parameter (Xu et al. arXiv:2502.00672, p.9 and p.13). The 'six processes' in the abstract are POST-HOC weighted-average aggregations of the 21 into interpretable groups. Do not conflate them.

rows.question: What is B-SOSE iteration-105's actual spatial extent and resolution?
rows.answer: 29.79S to 78S, NO equatorial data at all. Measured from the distributed grid.nc: YC max -29.789, YG max -29.945; coarsest dy 0.300 deg (at the northern edge), finest 0.070; dx 0.333 deg uniform; NY=294, NX=1080, NZ=52; TRAC06 on (time=60, Z=52, YC=294, XC=1080), monthly 2008-01-31 to 2012-12-30. It can only ever test southernoceanpac; eqpac needs TPOSE.

rows.question: What did the manuscript #1 adversarial red-team actually conclude?
rows.answer: 39 objections survived a grounded verify pass, 5 were killed (8-lens panel run as a 17-agent Workflow). The central claim — a parameter-specific identifiability map via a 0-D differentiable surrogate — SURVIVES, but only in qualified form. The panel's own read: 'nearly every attack is a conceded caveat left unpropagated to a headline, not a hidden defect.' The single highest-leverage fix is the joint-metric reconciliation.

rows.question: How much real dissolved silicate is actually available in-AOI, if we wanted a prognostic SiO2 box?
rows.answer: 6,968 QC-good GLODAPv3 bottles at the runner's <=50 m depth cut: eqpac 1,267 / natlsubpolar 4,364 / southernoceanpac 1,337. Against the 11 GEOTRACES bSi bottles currently in the loss (eqpac 7, natl 4, SO 0) that is a ~630x increase, and it takes the Southern Ocean from 0 to 1,337. Counted locally from D:\glodap\GLODAPv3_{Pacific,Atlantic}_Ocean.csv with silicatef==2.

rows.question: What is diatomgraz, physically?
rows.answer: A DIMENSIONLESS PALATABILITY MULTIPLIER on the predator-prey interaction, not a realized grazing rate. Dilution-experiment grazing rates map to it only through a predator/temperature/functional-response observation operator.

rows.question: Is the wind-channel R_PICPOC break DINN overfitting or a real confound?
rows.answer: A REAL confound. mld_wind gives R_PICPOC 0/10 at DANIELS_RPICPOC_W = 1, 3 AND 8, with the median stuck at 0.21. Up-weighting does not rescue it, which was the pre-declared decisive test (A4 vs A3). This justifies excluding wind on mechanistic, not tuning, grounds.

rows.question: Which literature citations are missing from the manuscript and which is most damaging?
rows.answer: A grep over main.tex finds transtrum, raue, gutenkunst, tagliabue, somes - and ZERO hits for schartau, ward, loptien/loeptien, kriest, mamnun, beven, or chis. The four that matter: Schartau et al. 2017 (10.5194/bg-14-1647-2017), Ward et al. 2010 (10.1016/j.jmarsys.2009.12.005), Loptien & Dietze 2017 (10.1002/2017GB005690) and Kriest et al. 2017 (verified half only). LOPTIEN & DIETZE IS THE DIRECT COMPARATOR - same synthetic-twin design, same question, opposite-polarity conclusion ('no meaningful best unique parameter set exists') - and not engaging it is the most likely single cause of a desk-level 'unaware of the relevant literature' review.

rows.question: What is alpfe, physically?
rows.answer: A near-unity scalar (0.928) applied to ALREADY-SOLUBLE iron, not a dust solubility. Darwin3's own docs say set it to 1 if the ironfile is already soluble, and v05 forces with the soluble Mahowald product. The 'iron dust solubility' mislabel was fixed in our code.

rows.question: What is actually blocking the Route B / GCM-validation path?
rows.answer: A scientific decision, not access or compute. None of the four observables has a spatial dimension in Darwin: ALPFE and SCAV_RAT are single global scalars in data.darwin &DARWIN_PARAMS; R_PICPOC and PALAT (diatomgraz) are 7-entry arrays over plankton type in data.traits &DARWIN_TRAITS. Our recovery is per-cell, so Route B needs a stated per-cell -> scalar reduction rule BEFORE any forward run - and the global-scalar configuration is exactly the one measured at 0/50 on the DOF ladder. Costs zero compute and gates every route.

rows.question: Why can an observations-only fit never become a cross-validated discovery with the current 0-D box?
rows.answer: A structural bind, independent of data volume. Per-cell DINN could in principle produce held-out spatial skill but has 3.9% observation coverage and a documented negative held-out result. Global scalar matches the data volume and is well-posed (6 weights vs 178 real residuals, over-determined ~30x) - but a spatially uniform parameter run through a 0-D box produces a spatially uniform anomaly, and held_out_obs.anomaly_masked_r2 scores against the constant train-basin mean, so a global scalar CANNOT beat that null by construction, at any data volume. The estimator that can pass cross-validation cannot be fit with the data; the estimator that can be fit cannot pass the test.

rows.question: Which new measurement best breaks the alpfe/scav_rat iron degeneracy (pooled 3-AOI)?
rows.answer: A surface particulate-Fe scavenging flux (234Th/210Po-derived): var_reduction 1434x on the 2x2 iron block, condition number 2930 -> 6.9. Subsurface dissolved Fe is essentially as powerful (1261x conditional, and the strongest at 24.8x fully marginalized, cond -> 2.5).

rows.question: Has "drop the ECCO-Darwin model output and fit observations only" (Jon's prescription) already been run? Do I need to build it?
rows.answer: ALREADY IMPLEMENTED AND ALREADY RUN TWICE, under the name *anchors-only*. n=10 (2026-07-21, PINN kept on, verify_run exit 0): alpfe 10/10, scav_rat 0/10, R_PICPOC 6/10, trio 0/10. n=50 (batch coord_anchors_pinnOFF, Slurm 8536393, verify_run --expect-seeds 50 exit 0, PINN also off): alpfe 50/50, R_PICPOC 28/50, scav_rat 0/50, diatomgraz 11/50, trio 0/50. Env recipe is DARWIN_PATTERN_W=0 POC_SUB_W=0 CHL1_W_EXTRA=0. The answer is 2-of-4. Do not re-derive.

rows.question: What fraction of the steady-state surface iron sink does scavenging carry at Carroll values?
rows.answer: About 79.7%. Biological uptake and the L1-L2 exchange carry the other 20.3% and are NOT homogeneous of degree one in the rate — which is why the alpfe/scav_rat gauge orbit is nearly flat rather than exactly flat. Co-scaling the pair by 16× moves steady-state surface DFe monotonically by 0.187 dex.

rows.question: Does the depth-resolved emulator beat persistence, and is the 'structural ceiling' story real?
rows.answer: Against a FREE per-cell seasonal AR(1) baseline the pooled skill is -0.146 [-0.20, -0.10] and the skill-vs-persistence CI straddles 0 - no significant skill anywhere in eqpac. Level skill vs persistence: DIC -0.844, ALK -1.149, PIC +0.210, POC +0.261, FeT -0.805, Chl1 -0.220. PIC/POC's apparent win is mechanical headroom (tend/anom 0.91-0.95), not learned dynamics.

rows.question: Is the trio 25/50 the same number as scav_rat's own leg?
rows.answer: Almost - they differ by one seed. scav_rat's own per-AOI leg is 26/50 at 2000 epochs; the joint >=2-of-3 trio is 25/50, one seed below. CLAUDE.md's '25/50' is the TRIO. At 4000 epochs both rise to ~41/50.

rows.question: Is any part of the eqpac/natl 'information limit' actually float32 roundoff?
rows.answer: Almost certainly not — the hypothesis is LARGELY DEFLATED by its own corrected arithmetic. The published 2930 is the Fisher eigenvalue ratio (sloppy 1.08e-3, stiff 3.18) and F ~ J^T J, so 2930 is ALREADY kappa(J)^2. Hence kappa(J)=54.1 and float32 retains 3.75 significant digits, not 0.29. The float64 rerun is downgraded from 'the decisive test' to a low-priority control (E7) where a null is the expected result. Still unaudited: the end-to-end training dtype (float32 confirmed only at carroll6_5pft_2layer.py:490).

rows.question: What happens if you drop ECCO-Darwin output and fit observations only (Jon's directive)?
rows.answer: Already run at n=50 (coord_anchors_pinnOFF, verify_run exit 0): alpfe 50/50 DECISIVE, R_PICPOC 28/50 decisive but halved, scav_rat 0/50 GONE (was 26/50), diatomgraz 11/50 below chance, joint trio 25/50 -> 0/50. scav_rat scores 40/50 cell-weighted but 0/50 per-AOI (always southernoceanpac only) - a textbook straddle trap.

rows.question: Was the non-positive Hessian eigenvalue at θ* a genuine indefiniteness (rank-deficiency) or an artifact?
rows.answer: An artifact of under-convergence, at the JOINT 3-AOI level. A 24-start global search gives eigenvalues [0.0, 0.0046, 0.0051, 0.093, 0.66, 2.29] — all ≥ 0, positive-semi-definite. The single zero direction is pure R_PICPOC (no calcite anchor in that config). Carroll itself IS a saddle of this objective (eigenvalues include −0.55, −0.051).

rows.question: Is alpfe / R_PICPOC recovery real, or is it pattern-matching against Darwin's own output fields?
rows.answer: Anchor-driven, not pattern-matching. With DARWIN_PATTERN_W=0, POC_SUB_W=0, CHL1_W_EXTRA=0 (every z-scored Darwin-output term off), alpfe recovers 10/10 per-AOI and R_PICPOC 6/10 per-AOI on real GEOTRACES iron + real Daniels calcite alone. n=10, 2000 epochs, verify_run exit 0 on 10/10 seeds, run D:/runs/anch_pinn. A separate PINN-OFF anchors-only n=50 run (Slurm 8536393, verify_run --expect-seeds 50 exit 0) gives alpfe 50/50 per-AOI (median 0.998), R_PICPOC 28/50, scav_rat 0/50 per-AOI (40/50 cell-weighted = southernoceanpac straddle), diatomgraz 11/50.

rows.question: Does the depth-resolved (3-D) BGC emulator work, and for which tracers?
rows.answer: Architecturally yes, scientifically mixed. B200 job 184411, 5 tracers x 5 levels, global 1 deg, cube [48,25,171,360], 250 epochs. Aggregate skill vs persistence +0.21, but per tracer: PIC +0.37/+0.40/+0.40/+0.39/+0.35 and POC +0.50/+0.51/+0.51/+0.50/+0.45 beat persistence at every depth, while DIC (-2.04 to -4.90), ALK (-3.39 to -7.77) and FeT (-2.27 to -3.51) do not. 10/25 channels beat persistence; the +0.21 aggregate is carried by PIC/POC and must not be reported alone. Skill is FLAT across depth for the predictable tracers, vindicating depth-as-channel (FNO2d over stacked levels, not FNO3d). Against a per-cell seasonal AR(1) baseline the same model is -0.161 +/- 0.015 across four seeds (doc carries a PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED banner saying exactly this).

rows.question: What does the 0-D box destroy, and what restores it? (NOTE: source doc is ARCHIVED 2026-07-24, superseded by docs/findings/2026-07-24_bgc_operator_lineage_synthesis.md §5. The LEGITIMACY question itself remains OPEN - it is posed to a math expert, not answered.)
rows.answer: At spatially-uniform parameters the box relaxes to a near-uniform state (tracer coefficient of variation ~1e-15) whereas the full model has O(1) spatial structure - so box-vs-model PATTERN correlations are not fidelity metrics. Structure is restored by making parameters spatially varying: per-cell recovers the trio 7/10 where a single global parameter vector recovers 0/10.

rows.question: Where does the DINN method come from, and who is the closest concurrent work?
rows.answer: BINN, Xu et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.00672): small MLP predicts parameters from environmental covariates -> sigmoid-to-physical-range -> differentiable CLM5 forward model -> end-to-end backprop. DINN is the marine adaptation; PINN (Raissi et al. 2019) is the grandparent. Neural-BGC (Ouala & Lachkar 2026) is a pure-NN emulator of DO/NO3 with no parameters in the Darwin sense - methodological overlap zero. Carroll's Green's functions = +/-20% perturbations, ~12 model runs per Gauss-Newton step.

rows.question: Which direction does the arithmetic collapse bias the scav_rat count?
rows.answer: BOTH, depending on the basin. arithmetic = geometric x exp(sigma^2/2), so the direction is set by where the geometric centre sits in the 0.60x-1.40x band. natlsubpolar sits at 0.43x Carroll, below the band, and the inflation carries it up across the edge - manufacturing passes (5 -> 19/50). The single-AOI Southern Ocean sits at 0.73x, inside the band, and the same inflation carries it out past the top (49 -> 30/50) - so the arithmetic collapse UNDERSTATES the one basin where scav_rat is established. Under the geometric collapse scav_rat is biased LOW everywhere (0.43x-0.89x Carroll).

rows.question: Is alpfe's quoted ~8% precision a measurement, or the distance from its upper bound to Carroll?
rows.answer: BOUND GEOMETRY, measured. Job 276927, four arms x 50 seeds in one submission. The trained fit rails to whatever ceiling it is given: median 0.9967 against a 1.0 bound (99.7% of it) and 1.5940 against a 1.6 bound (99.6% of it). alpfe carries NO upper-side information. Because its upper bound sits at rel 0.077 from Carroll, INSIDE the 0.40 band, a railed fit scores as recovered regardless of the data, so the 49/50 is substantially the bound's doing: widening the ceiling takes it to 0/50. What survives is the DIRECTION - 49/50 against an untrained 10/50 at bound 1.0 - so the data says alpfe is high but does not say it is 0.93. Do not quote 7.6% or 8% as an accuracy.

rows.question: Which Track-2 numbers are actually backed by a committed artifact file?
rows.answer: Backed: physics_3d.json, de3d_ensemble.json, de_eqpac_ensemble.json, eqpac_ctl_{linear,log}.json, d3_ctl_log.json, rollout_dtscale.json, rollout_flagship_ctl.json. NOT backed — six cited files are absent from the worktree and main checkout: diff_surf.json, diff_3d.json, diff_daily_eqpac.json, matched_k1.json, matched_k8.json, opt_physics.json. Every diffusion number in this project is currently unbacked, as is the entire k1-vs-k8 horizon table.

rows.question: Why is scav_rat recoverable in the Southern Ocean and not elsewhere?
rows.answer: Because of DEPTH, not the basin. Single-AOI southernoceanpac, volume-matched arms: surface-only iron (13 bins) gives scav_rat 14/50 (not above chance), subsurface-only iron (14 bins) gives 33/50 (RECOVERS), both against untrained null 0/50. Fisher exact two-sided P = 0.000268. `verify_run` exit 0 on all four arms, GATE_FAIL=0 (jobs 239556 + 239560). The SO is simply where subsurface GEOTRACES coverage and a strong sink coincide.

rows.question: When exactly does the ECCO-Darwin v05 daily archive end, and why did two statements conflict?
rows.answer: Both were right. The archive provides daily means for 1992-01-01 through 2018-12-30, in files stamped by their INTERVAL-END iteration 72 through 709992. The last file's .meta gives timeInterval = [8.519040000000E+08, 8.519904000000E+08] = days 9860.0–9861.0, i.e. a 24-hour average over 2018-12-30 stamped 2018-12-31 00:00. The HTTP 500 at iter 710064 was also correct. State the AVERAGING WINDOW, not the stamp — they differ by one day.

rows.question: Is the recoverability gap an optimization problem or an information problem?
rows.answer: Both, and it decomposes: a largely closeable optimization component (scav_rat 25/50 -> 41/50 at 4000 epochs, natl 20 -> 40) plus a residual information component (eqpac 6/50, the sole basin more compute cannot fix).

rows.question: Which paper venue should the Track-2 workshop submission target?
rows.answer: CCAI, not 'AI for Stochastic Dynamics' — 'recommendation reverses to CCAI, unless diffusion is re-run'. The 'diffusion adds no skill' paper rests on four missing artifacts and cannot be written honestly without re-running EDM diffusion; the 'metrics are blind to invalidating defects' paper is fully backed on both load-bearing legs.

rows.question: What is the load-bearing mechanism behind per-cell recovery - capacity, per-cell resolution, or something else?
rows.answer: CROSS-AOI POOLING. Removing only the weight sharing destroys the result while ADDING 812 parameters. Corroborated by main's causal control (commit 57ee408, 2000 ep, n=10, verify_run exit 0): the Southern Ocean R_PICPOC leg moves 1.27x -> 13.06x Carroll when the anchor is removed, in a basin with ZERO Daniels observations in either arm, so it cannot be responding to data it never had; per-AOI 10/10 -> 2/10.

rows.question: How does one DINN training epoch scale with cell count and step count on an H200?
rows.answer: Cell count is essentially FREE; step count is linear. Measured median wall-clock of one DINN->integrate->loss->backward epoch on an H200 (139.8 GB), torch.compile'd per step: at 200 steps, 2,853 cells = 38.5 ms and 105,300 cells = 42.4 ms (per-cell-step falls 67.47 -> 2.01 ns). Per-step cost is 0.192-0.212 ms regardless of grid size. Steps scale linearly: 10,000 cells at 200/400/800/1600 steps = 41.5/83.7/166.9/332.6 ms. Fit t = a + b*cells @200 steps: a = 40.9 ms, b = 17.5 ns/cell, R2 = 0.2142 (n=8) - the low R2 is the point, the epoch is dominated by fixed launch overhead.

rows.question: Which real observable constrains which parameter, measured on the real loss at Carroll?
rows.answer: Clean one-to-one. realiron (GEOTRACES dissolved Fe): alpfe Fisher 2.60e-01 / CRLB 68.5, scav_rat 5.40e-01 / 78.2 - roughly 500x tighter than the next parameter. realbsi (biogenic Si): diatomgraz 8.16e-01 / CRLB 3,530 - roughly 38x tighter than the next. realdaniels: R_PICPOC 7.40e-01 / CRLB 1.353, all five others pinned at 0.994-1.000 of the ridge floor. Smallgrow and Biggrow have no real observable at all - that absence IS the finding.

rows.question: When a chance baseline has been measured as a sample, which statistical test applies?
rows.answer: Compare samples with Fisher exact. Reserve the rule-of-three floor (3/N) for a genuinely UNOBSERVED null rate. Quoting the floor where a measured sample exists systematically understates the evidence - it flattered us on the anchor-off control (binomial 0.078 vs Fisher exact 0.0133). This is now a standing rule.

rows.question: What are the correct chance rates for the >=2-of-3 metric actually graded?
rows.answer: Compound the single-draw rates with 3p^2(1-p)+p^3: alpfe 0.450, scav_rat 0.071, Smallgrow 0.189, Biggrow 0.087, diatomgraz 0.543, R_PICPOC 0.0015; joint-trio null ~4e-5. main.tex:1143-1155 gives SINGLE-DRAW rates and :1154 instructs the reader to run the wrong test. Note these compounded values are BOUNDS - AOI outcomes are not independent within a seed (one network, one fit). The error runs in our favour: R_PICPOC's null drops 15x.

rows.question: Can we self-run ECCO-Darwin v05 on AICR?
rows.answer: Compute yes, data no. The published 767-rank decomposition exceeds the 512-CPU QOS ceiling on every partition; a 468-rank re-tile at 45x45 builds (RETILE_BUILD_OK, job 227523) and the 286-entry blanklist can simply be dropped. But two of four required input trees (nbp19_dmenemen_public_llc270, era_xx) are NOT public and ecco.jpl.nasa.gov refuses TCP:443 from four independent vantage points. 49 GB / 140 files staged.

rows.question: Was 'no published number was corrupted' by the per-AOI grader bug?
rows.answer: Correct, CORRUPTION AUDIT CLEAN. Four independent grader implementations agree on ctrl_n50 (49 / 26 / 2 / 50, trio 25/50). The single-AOI bug was latent: grade_all_params.py:105 and contract_report.py:119 hardcoded >= 2 for the per-AOI majority, grading every SINGLE-AOI run 0/n. A second bug, grade_all_params.py:192, had a backslash in an f-string (SyntaxError below Python 3.12). The per-AOI majority rule has EIGHT implementations, two of which were wrong.

rows.question: Why is the Southern Ocean rank 2/4 in the identifiability probe?
rows.answer: Coverage for TWO observables, not one. The two SO nulls are R_PICPOC (exact 0 - no Daniels coverage) and diatomgraz (8e-7 - the SO has ZERO bSi/POSi bins). Only the iron pair (alpfe, scav_rat) is constrained there. The eqpac/natl ordering soft->stiff is alpfe < scav_rat < R_PICPOC < diatomgraz, with diatomgraz stiffest where bSi exists.

rows.question: Is scav_rat's Southern Ocean signal surface curvature or depth structure?
rows.answer: DEPTH. Volume-matched head-to-head: so_sub (subsurface iron only, 14 bins) 33/50 against null 0/50, P(>=k)=1.70e-28, RECOVERS; so_surf (surface only, 13 bins) 14/50, not above chance. Fisher exact two-sided P = 0.000268. The falsifier cleared: alpfe is 49/50 in so_surf, so that arm fits fine. The levels identify DIFFERENT parameters — surface iron gives alpfe 49/50 and scav_rat 14/50; subsurface gives alpfe 14/50 and scav_rat 33/50. Removing the surface term costs nothing (McNemar vs parent P=0.69, 11 lost / 14 gained).

rows.question: Is the scalar R_PICPOC recoverable, or is that the same question as the Omega-modulation one?
rows.answer: DIFFERENT SCOPES, keep them separate. The SCALAR R_PICPOC is ALREADY recoverable - Track-1 lands it approximately at Carroll's value once the contaminated Southern-Ocean ratio target is sanitized. What real data cannot constrain is whether an ENVIRONMENTAL DRIVER MODULATES it (the closure ratio = R0 * Omega^n).

rows.question: Can we train the parameter learner or emulator on daily v05 data?
rows.answer: Daily is a decisive negative for the PARAMETER LEARNER (job 235995): anomaly variance fraction is the same daily as monthly (SST 0.113 vs 0.134, surfChl1 0.761 vs 0.756, surfChl2 0.777 vs 0.771) and daily lag-1 r of 0.994-0.996 gives n_eff of about 17 to 24 out of ~8,700 steps, FEWER than the 158 monthly steps already in hand. Also, the daily archive has NO DIC, ALK, PIC, POC or FeT (17 dirs, 15 unique fields, all surface), so the current prognostic set cannot be trained daily. The emulator half stays OPEN: the pre-existing artifact is contaminated four ways and its +0.408 is a linear-space number that does not survive a log-space re-score.

rows.question: How does Darwin's surface iron compare to B-SOSE in the Southern Ocean?
rows.answer: Darwin fet_binned median 0.197 nM (IQR 0.178-0.217) vs B-SOSE TRAC06 at Z=-2.1 m median 0.165 nM (IQR 0.153-0.176); ratio 1.21 (IQR 1.10-1.34); log10 spatial r = 0.676 over 21,120 matched cells. Robust to matching scheme (1x1 / 3x3 / 7x7 / 15x15 give ratio 1.211/1.211/1.210/1.208 and r 0.676/0.677/0.681/0.689).

rows.question: Why was the particulate:dissolved iron ratio retracted as a route to the scavenging rate?
rows.answer: Deductively: the ratio reduces to scavenging rate x POC / sinking rate, so dissolved iron cancels EXACTLY. Empirically: in GEOTRACES IDP2025 surface data only 76 samples worldwide carry both total particulate and dissolved iron under strict co-location, 4 of them in the eqpac box, and where both exist the ratio spans ~2.6 orders of magnitude. Caveat flagged in the doc's own pre-send checklist: the 76/4 counts are a floor on co-location, not a count of ocean locations, and were not re-confirmed.

rows.question: Should the depth-resolved emulator use FNO3d or depth-as-channel?
rows.answer: Depth-as-channel (FNO2d over stacked levels), for both PoC and global production. v05 levels are irregular variable-thickness (2.5 m to 6000 m) so a Fourier transform along z is ill-posed, and every production ocean emulator does the same: Samudra (arXiv 2412.03795) puts 19 depth levels as channels of a 2D ConvNeXt-UNet (135M params, 158 in / 154 out channels, 150x faster than OM4); SamudrACE (arXiv 2509.12490) uses 145 2D fields across 8 atmospheric + 19 oceanic levels. FNO3d is a Phase-3 research probe only.

rows.question: Which gradient strategy for the Track-2 Phase-1 differentiable transport UDE?
rows.answer: Discretise-then-optimise: plain PyTorch autograd through the existing checkpointed RK4 integrate(), giving exact gradients of the actual discrete loss. Explicitly REJECT continuous/backsolve adjoint (torchdiffeq odeint_adjoint) as the primary path - documented unstable on stiff/PDE-like systems. Memory from windowed BPTT (30-90 simulated days, detached ICs) plus nested Revolve-style checkpointing (~3650 daily steps -> ~60 stored states at ~2-3x recompute).

rows.question: Which phase of the GP15 Po/Pb data is usable in eqpac?
rows.answer: Dissolved (D), not total. Within eqpac: phase T has 3 finite samples of 67, surface (0 m) only, 3 stations; phase D has 64 of 67, depths 20-5340 m, 3 stations. load_scavenging_anchor DEFAULTS to phase='T', so wiring it in with the default gives an almost-empty anchor in the one basin that matters, with no error. Pinned by test_the_dissolved_phase_is_the_usable_one. Honest limit: only three stations - the informative content is depth structure, not horizontal coverage.

rows.question: What should the identifiability-contract contribution claim actually be?
rows.answer: Do not write 'we introduce' or 'methodological contribution' anywhere near the untrained baseline or the contract. Concede the operation, keep the application, name the parents first. What remains defensible, narrowly: (1) applying a null control to a BINARY pass/fail recovery count so that tolerance metric's chance rate is measured not assumed; (2) the fail-closed UNAVAILABLE convention wired to an exit code (noting PROBAST does something stronger); (3) the NUMBERS themselves - diatomgraz scores 0.640 untrained, which retired one of our own headline results. Cite Guillaume et al. 2019 as the closest existing statement of what the contract mechanises.

rows.question: How does Earth2Studio encode ocean depth, and what does our wrapper have to fix?
rows.answer: E2S has no first-class depth dimension - depth is baked into the variable NAME (DIC_k0, DIC_k1, ... Chl1_kZ), tensor layout [batch, variable, lat, lon], canonical coord order batch, time, lead_time, variable, lat, lon. Three conformance bugs in DarwinEmulator (emulator.py:174-207): (1) lead_time_h float-hours must become an accumulating np.timedelta64 lead_time; (2) input_coords advertises only (variable, lat, lon) - missing batch/time and wrong order; (3) create_iterator is bounded and the entry point is step, but E2S wants an unbounded generator and __call__. Also: E2S fetch_data regrids lat/lon only and map_coords REFUSES curvilinear LLC grids, so all depth remapping and LLC->regular regridding must happen inside the DataSource.

rows.question: What is the honest GHG-Center / carbon-MRV motivation for this work?
rows.answer: ECCO-Darwin CO2 flux is a NASA-hosted, CC-BY carbon-MRV-relevant product whose worth is its calibration. But the global sink is only ~2% biology (Carroll 2022), so identifiability matters for regional/seasonal biological-pump credibility - where the Carroll-6 were actually tuned - NOT for the headline sink. Flagged overclaims to avoid: quantifying a flux-error budget without an OSSE, and attributing verified OAE credits to the hosted product.

rows.question: Which recovery counts could be rail-to-bound artifacts, and is R_PICPOC one of them?
rows.answer: EXACTLY TWO, and R_PICPOC is NOT one. A count can be a rail-to-bound artifact precisely when a bound lies inside the pass band, which is arithmetic on the registry and needs no run. alpfe (rel hi 0.077) and diatomgraz (rel hi 0.205) qualify; scav_rat (0.950/3.979), Smallgrow (0.849/2.026), Biggrow (0.768/3.635) and R_PICPOC (0.882/34.336) do not. R_PICPOC is therefore EXONERATED by arithmetic: no railed fit can land inside its band, so its 50/50 cannot be bound geometry. alpfe is confirmed by experiment; diatomgraz is untested and already fails on prior contamination. Shipped as contract.bound_proximity_risk.

rows.question: What is BINN's '50x faster than MCMC' claim actually measuring?
rows.answer: End-to-end TRAINING time against PRODA (per-site adaptive-Metropolis MCMC), single CPU, 2,000 profiles: PRODA 577.7 h, BINN matrix 52.5 h (~11x), BINN vectorized 10.5 h (~57x). Not inference time - inference is a single MLP forward pass. Training data: 25,925 SOC profiles / 169,104 measurements from WoSIS.
rows.doc: LOCAL-ONLY source, not in the repo: 2026-05-03_overnight.md

rows.question: Is capacity, diffusion, or ensembling the lever for the emulator?
rows.answer: Ensembling. An 8-seed deep ensemble lifts a comparable monthly 3-D run +0.432 -> +0.484; EDM diffusion adds no skill and HURTS on 3-D (+0.421 -> +0.395); ~4x parameters bought +0.007. Do not build bigger - ensemble.

rows.question: Did the numerically-dead surfChl4 channel poison daily training?
rows.answer: Essentially no - the hypothesis is a null. log4 (surfChl4 removed) beats log5 by 0.0046 against a seed sd of about 0.0016: consistent in sign across all three seed pairs, so a real effect, but about 1.3% of the remaining gap. Log space carries essentially all of the effect and the dead channel carries none of it.

rows.question: What are the loss-weight whitening semantics, and what do the weights implicitly assert?
rows.answer: Every absolute-units block divides its masked MSE by scale = mean(target^2) over its own mask - 11 sites (lines 1719, 1725, 1741, 1751, 1760, 1774, 1786, 1802, 1821, 1826, 1847). So each block enters as a FRACTIONAL-error term and w_g is 1/sigma_g^2 in fractional units. Nothing measured any of them; every one was set by sweep. Consequence: GEOTRACES_W=0.3 vs GEOTRACES_SUB_W=1.0 asserts surface bottle dFe is 1.8x fractionally noisier than subsurface; DANIELS_RPICPOC_W=1.0 asserts a CP:PP incubation ratio is as fractionally precise as a bottle dFe measurement, which it is not. Dropping the Darwin targets does not fix this - it RAISES the stakes, because the anchor weights then are the entire loss.

rows.question: At n=50, how large a drop from 30/50 is statistically detectable?
rows.answer: Exact two-sided Fisher: 25/50 → P=0.4216 (no), 22/50 → 0.1609 (no), 20/50 → 0.0713 (NO), 18/50 → 0.0272 (P<0.05), 15/50 → 0.0046 (P<0.01), 12/50 → 0.0005. The P<0.05 boundary is at 18-19/50, not 20. 'Not significantly different from 30/50' must never be reported as 'unchanged'.

rows.question: How many ocean products does the US GHG Center host?
rows.answer: Exactly one. Confirmed against the live STAC collections API on 2026-07-24: 29 collections total, eccodarwin-co2flux-monthgrid-v5 is the SOLE ocean/marine one (all others land/atmosphere/methane/biomass).

rows.question: Which input tree is missing for a v05 run, and is our access the problem?
rows.answer: Exactly one: era_xx / era_xx_it42_v2 (atmospheric forcing) plus nbp19_dmenemen_public_llc270 are not on the public NAS portal. They live on ECCO Drive, which is Earthdata-gated and NOT SERVING - TCP:443 refused from four independent vantage points since 2026-07-28 while podaac.jpl, urs.earthdata and nas.nasa.gov all return 200. The host is down; this is not an access problem. Whether an ordinary Earthdata registrant can read ECCO2/LLC270/era_xx_it42_v2 specifically is unverified.

rows.question: How degenerate is the equatorial Pacific on its own?
rows.answer: Far more than the pooled problem: condition number 12545.4 (not 2930), sloppy/stiff eigenvalues 4.726e-05 / 5.929e-01, and posterior corr(alpfe, scav_rat) = +1.000 exactly. It is the degenerate basin, quantified.

rows.question: Which emulator tracer is the genuine failure, and why?
rows.answer: FeT - the only tracer that beats NO baseline: persistence -0.805, damped -0.869, seasonal clim -0.329, anomaly-persistence -1.054, annual-clim anomaly-R2 -0.138. Yet corr_tend is +0.367, the signature of missing forcing (episodic dust deposition and scavenging are not in the prognostic-only input set). The fix is an input channel, not a bigger network.

rows.question: How many GEOTRACES surface samples carry BOTH particulate and dissolved iron (i.e. can support a partitioning observable)?
rows.answer: Fe_TP+Fe_D: 76 global / 4 on eqpac. Fe_TPL+Fe_D: 130 global / 0 on eqpac. Fe_D alone is dense: 4,472 surface (~24k all-depth). Where both are measured the ratio spans 2.59 dex (Fe_TP) / 3.7 dex (Fe_TPL).

rows.question: If a perturbed-parameter ensemble ever becomes affordable, how should the emulator be conditioned?
rows.answer: FiLM (feature-wise scale-and-shift per layer), which beats input-concatenation by roughly an order of magnitude when the parameter changes the operator, and trained on true Jacobian labels (derivative-informed, SC-FNO / DIFNO) — never plain output-MSE. Recorded as the design default, contingent on the ensemble.

rows.question: Is the iron source/sink degeneracy specific to our box, or field-wide?
rows.answer: Field-wide. Tagliabue 2016 FeMIP Table 2, all 13 models: concentration agreed to ~2x, residence time roams 169x, decomposing as ~130x input flux x ~1.3x inventory; the sedimentary iron source spans 0 to 194 Gmol/yr with every model landing near 0.5 nM by compensating with scavenging. The contribution is not discovering the degeneracy but naming it as a formal identifiability/sloppiness problem.

rows.question: Is the explicit vertical-diffusion CFL wall fixed, and what was the failure mode?
rows.answer: Fixed. Explicit vertical_diffusion is stable only for kz·dt/dz² < 0.5 and silently NaNs above it; realistic mixed-layer kz ≈ 1e-2 m²/s gives r = 2.16 at dz=10 m, dt=0.25 d. thomas_solve + vertical_diffusion_implicit (backward Euler) removes the limit: matches dense torch.linalg.solve to 1e-16, mass drift ~1e-15, gradcheck-clean. H200-validated: at r=2.16 explicit blows up 1.16e34× while imex stays at 0.88×; checkpoint == plain bit-identical on GPU; 327k-cell grid fwd+bwd in 1.1 s. Commits a0e7a50 + 862f319, suite 376 passed.

rows.question: Which observables does each of the two operating points hold?
rows.answer: Flagship geo1 (full loss) holds {alpfe 49/50, scav_rat 25/50, R_PICPOC 50/50} with diatomgraz open. MLD + heavy-Daniels (arm1_mld_dan8, anchors-only) holds {alpfe, diatomgraz, R_PICPOC} 10/10/10 with scav_rat 1/10. alpfe is 10/10 everywhere. No single config holds all four per-AOI.

rows.question: Which repo numbers cannot currently be verified from a committed artifact?
rows.answer: Four, found while checking. (1) The negative held-out R2 for the box is PRINT-ONLY: runner :1971-1990 computes and prints it, but the result JSON (:2073-2136) records neither GEOTRACES_HOLDOUT_FRAC nor the R2; a grep of docs/**/*.json returns no held-out R2. (2) covar_env_common.sh is not in the repo - POSI_W=1 in the flagship is INFERRED from the dgchl row overriding it to 0, not read. (3) scav_rat per-AOI is 25 in some places and 26 in others (2026-07-21_joint_number_reconciliation.md tables 26 at line 15 and 25 at line 28) - one is wrong by one seed. (4) The alpfe null hit-rate 0.47 appears only in docs/project_checkpoint_2026-07-25.md:31 with no backing artifact.

rows.question: What is the pre-registered rule for the parameterisation ladder (free pointwise field vs DINN)?
rows.answer: Free field WORSE than DINN -> the network regularises and 'per-cell architecture is load-bearing' is earned. EQUAL -> scope to per-cell STRUCTURE and drop 'architecture' from STATUS and the abstract. BETTER -> degrees of freedom are doing the work, report it first. The metric is per-AOI recovery against Carroll, NOT training loss (the free field is expected to fit training loss better). Until it lands, say 'structure', not 'architecture'.

rows.question: Which published calibration methods were considered for this project and correctly rejected, and what blocks each?
rows.answer: GF calibration engine (single v05 realization); BINN's 25,925-profile amortization, two-point/covariance statistics, and SINDy for Track-1 (dimensional 0-D gap); KOH/BACCO GP emulator, history-matching PPE waves, full-state EnKF, CES/EKI as recovery (single realization / rank-1 null); continuous reverse-time adjoint (unstable for stiff advection — use checkpointed discrete adjoint); NeuralGCM long-rollout CRPS (single realization + 1-step info ceiling).

rows.question: Would a prognostic silicate cycle (GLODAPv3 dissolved SiO2) fix the bSi circularity, and what does it cost?
rows.answer: GLODAPv3 silicate is available (columns silicate/silicatef/silicateqc, umol/kg; 822,326 QC-good values across Pacific + Atlantic, 39,676 at <=10 m) but using it needs a prognostic SiO2 state: 15 -> 17 tracers, invalidating every darwin_ic_cache_*.npz, plus an f_Si co-limitation term and a GLODAPv3 bottle loader. Multi-day; a follow-on, not a precondition.

rows.question: Is the R_PICPOC covariate break wind-specific or generic?
rows.answer: Generic to carbonate/salinity channels. The single-covariate matrix shows SSS, pCO2atm and CO2flux ALL break R_PICPOC too. MLD (mixing) is uniquely safe.

rows.question: How many real co-located GEOTRACES iron observations exist for an iron UDE?
rows.answer: IDP2025 surface, good-QC, co-located particulate AND dissolved: 76 pairs globally and 4 in eqpac, over a pFe/DFe ratio span of 2.594 dex. A 67-weight ScavClosure against 4 eqpac points is ~17 weights per observation. STATUS.md:520 puts the dissolved field at ~14 surface cells for ~10k native cells, and higher resolution makes this worse, not better.

rows.question: What alpfe does independent, non-Darwin dust data imply, and where is the anchor valid?
rows.answer: In the dust-dominated Saharan N. Atlantic (10-30N, 45-20W) the Xu & Weber 2021 Al-inverse soluble-Fe deposition (0.0211) divided by v05's prescribed Mahowald deposition (0.0183 mmol Fe/m2/yr) implies alpfe = 1.15, against Carroll's 0.93; across the Fe:Al molar range 0.08-0.20 the implied value spans ~0.61-1.53, bracketing Carroll cleanly. Off-region it is 2.36 (natl), 2.86 (sopac), 8.66 (eqpac). Ensemble spread ranks anchor quality: natl 0.30 < SO 0.44 < Saharan 0.54 < eqpac 0.88. This 1.15 is the value distilled into DUST_ANCHOR_MU.

rows.question: Is our carbonate / Omega solver independently validated, or is it same-model circular?
rows.answer: Independently validated against community-standard PyCO2SYS on 2000 real GLODAPv3 surface points: r(Omega) = 0.9999, r(log Omega) = 1.0000, log-log slope 0.98, median |rel diff| 1.3% (a constant ~1.4% bias, harmless to the slope-based oracle). Artifact docs/findings/carbonate_pyco2sys_validation.json, script scripts/validate_carbonate_pyco2sys.py, commit 51e2cb0.

rows.question: What does '50/50 recovered' actually mean in accuracy terms?
rows.answer: Inside +/-40%, NOT accurate. Median relative error: alpfe 7.6% flagship / 6.1% obs-only; scav_rat 33% / 46%; R_PICPOC 22% / 32%; diatomgraz 60% / 11%. R_PICPOC is 46/50 Cal-grade but only 1/50 Excellent. Always report relative error alongside pass/fail bands.

rows.question: What is the DOF ladder for the trio, and does capacity help?
rows.answer: Inverted U, and capacity along a flat direction hurts: 6 free values -> trio 0/50; 406 shared -> 25/50; 1218 per-AOI -> 3/50; 17,106 free per-cell -> 0/40.
