rows.answer: No, keep it OUT. Under Darwin's fixed ligand it is a deterministic function of DFe and adds zero rank. Only INDEPENDENT ligand data (CLE-AdCSV) would help.

rows.question: Does the pre-fix calendar bug (delta_t 1200s) change the daily emulator headline?
rows.answer: No, measured not assumed. Both scorings (cube time axis vs time rederived from iters at delta_t=1200s) give bitwise-identical overall numbers, because persistence and ar1_percell are calendar-free by construction and ar1_percell is the winning baseline everywhere. Seasonal baselines do move (seasonal_clim -0.11 to -0.68; ar1_seasonal_percell +0.013 to +0.046).

rows.question: Would post-hoc bias correction extend the emulator's horizon?
rows.answer: No, measured not assumed. Raw one-step error RMS 0.3112 (58% of saturation); ||b_field|| 0.0213 (6.8%), ||b_chan|| 0.0043 (1.4%). Subtracting b_field makes rollout WORSE beyond step 2 (-0.377 vs -0.305 at step 6) because 58.7M values estimated from 110 samples fit noise.

rows.question: Is the scientific novelty of the Track-1 identifiability study high?
rows.answer: No, minimal. Parameter identifiability in marine ecosystem models is an established field (Biogeosciences bg-14-1647-2017); AD-for-parameter-inference is old (AD Model Builder); the native adjoint is ECCO v4; BGC observing-system design exists (Argo OSSEs); the iron degeneracy is Frants 2016. The defensible METHODOLOGICAL novelty is the narrow combination: a differentiable 0-D surrogate as an inversion-side identifiability and observation-design probe for a non-differentiable GCM, stated 'to our knowledge' against those five prior works.

rows.question: Are the per-PFT surface chlorophyll fields usable as targets?
rows.answer: No, not until TRAC27-TRAC31 are resolved against Darwin's tracer table. surfChl4 is NEGATIVE in 100% of ocean cells at the median timestep; surfChl5 41.3%, surfChl3 39.7%, surfChl2 26.5%, surfChl1 9.4%. Negatives persist all 27 years, so this is not spin-up. Log-space training needs clipping and the clipped fraction must be recorded. SST (26.1% negative, min -1.961 C, max 33.08 C) is physical and validates the pipeline end to end. Carry forward: surfChl4 should never appear as a target again (linear skill -606 is a division by noise).

rows.question: Should we ingest real Schmoker 2013 dilution-grazing data to anchor diatomgraz?
rows.answer: No, not yet. Two prerequisites first: (1) a finer profile grid that brackets theta*=0.83 (the current [0.05..1.0] grid skips it, argmin lands on the upper edge at 1.0, valid:false, bracketed:false), and (2) a box with grazer structure. The 0-D box has no grazer-biomass tracer, so the size-fraction contrast the anchor is meant to exploit is trivially satisfied, not faithfully tested.

rows.question: Is rel_span a calibrated identifiability threshold?
rows.answer: No, on two independent grounds. (a) It is BOUNDS-DEPENDENT: the profile grid is torch.logspace over PARAM_BOUNDS, so widening the physical prior mechanically raises rel_span and can flip FLAT to CURVED with no new data (the repo already documents the fragility: iron_scav_rat_profile.json reports 25x / 32x / 100x at thresholds 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.05). (b) It has NO DISTRIBUTIONAL MEANING: Raue's classification is a threshold-crossing test against chi-squared(alpha, df) on a calibrated likelihood, but our objective is a weighted MSE with AOI weights plus ratio and positivity terms, so no chi-squared quantile is available. Demote rel_span to a descriptive statistic.

rows.question: Does adding prognostic SiO2 + Si-limitation make diatomgraz identifiable?
rows.answer: No, parity, and the earlier claim was overstated. With growth fixed, prognostic-SiO2 and the circular-bSi arm self-recover diatomgraz identically (0.829 vs 0.830); with growth marginalized both show the SAME growth-grazing compensation ridge (rel_span 3.36 vs 3.31). Sell the ~40-line SiO2 addition as a DEFENSIBILITY win - it retires the reviewer M11 circularity criticism and unlocks ~630x more real observations (~6,968 GLODAP silicate bottles vs 11 bSi) - NOT as an identifiability fix. diatomgraz stays non-identifiable on real data; the growth-grazing ridge is the true obstacle.

rows.question: Is 'nobody has a global ocean-BGC neural operator' still true?
rows.answer: No, partially FALSE as of 2026. BG4Sea (Mercator Ocean, global ML emulator of NEMO-PISCES, seasonal horizon) is the competitor to name; also global surface chl-a (Biogeosciences 23:2601, 2026), a 1-D prognostic 52-var ERSEM emulator with built-in C/N/P conservation (arXiv:2606.27168), and GOBAI-O2 (ESSD 18:287, 2026). The residual gap is real but thin and must be stated narrowly.

rows.question: Is v05 chlorophyll globally biased low?
rows.answer: No, regime-specific. Equatorial Pacific bias is -0.077 dex (0.84x), 95% CI [-0.090, -0.064], INSIDE the 0.130 dex noise floor, RMSE 0.122 dex, n = 192 months, satellite coverage 98.6% mean / 90.9% min, zero v05 cells clipped. The subpolar N. Atlantic is -0.696 dex (5.0x low), CI [-0.787, -0.617], RMSE 0.912 dex, 159,014 cells clipped. The correct statement is 'unbiased in the oligotrophic regime and 5x low in the bloom regime'.

rows.question: Is 'the box is tuning-exhausted — a positive result needs new observations, not more GPU' still the standing verdict?
rows.answer: No, retired, and the retirement is APPLIED (STATUS.md:593 records the earlier box-tuning-exhausted verdict as superseded). Two components: a large CLOSEABLE OPTIMIZATION component (scav_rat 25 -> 41/50 at 4000 epochs, natl 20 -> 40, no new data, job 190529) plus a residual INFORMATION component (eqpac 6/50). Compute is no longer a no-op.

rows.question: Is the alpfe/scav_rat degeneracy exact?
rows.answer: No, sloppy not structural. In the shipped 2-layer box at Carroll values, scavenging carries 79.7% of the steady-state surface iron sink; biological uptake and L1-L2 exchange carry the other 20.3% and neither is homogeneous in r0. Co-scaling the pair by 16x moves steady-state surface DFe monotonically by 0.187 dex. Nearly flat, not flat.

rows.question: Can the 93% vs 98.3% Menemenlis discrepancy be reconciled?
rows.answer: No, still unreconciled and now less important. Raw-cost arithmetic gives 98.3%; the slide annotates 93%; 93% could not be reproduced from any anchor row. NEITHER number should carry the argument. Quote the raw costs, show the subtraction, state the depth caveat.

rows.question: Is the LLC facet/cube-seam artifact observable in our emulator?
rows.answer: No, structurally. emulator_poc.py:352-366 regrids native (face,j,i) onto a flat lat/lon array via binned_statistic_2d BEFORE the FNO, so the facet-seam topology is discarded for every cube we build. The named artifact is unobservable by construction; the antimeridian seam-fold arithmetic was also verified correct.

rows.question: Does giving the parameter learner more degrees of freedom improve recovery?
rows.answer: No, the DOF ladder is an INVERTED U and the peak is at the sharing architecture, not the largest one. Trio per-AOI: global scalar (6 values) 0/50; shared DINN (406) 25/50; per-AOI DINN (3 x 406 = 1218) 3/50; free per-cell field (17,106) 0/40. peraoi_dinn is ARCHITECTURALLY IDENTICAL to the flagship - same class, same n_input_channels=1, same hidden_dim, same 406 weights per net - the only change is per-AOI copies instead of sharing, and that alone takes the trio 25/50 -> 3/50 and scav_rat 26/50 -> 4/50 despite 3x more free parameters.

rows.question: Do alpfe and R_PICPOC rest on Darwin's pickup initial condition?
rows.answer: No, the IC half of the Darwin dependency is CLOSED. With a literature IC and no MLD (obsonly_litic): alpfe 50/50 (P = 1.13e-35, k* = 16) and R_PICPOC 32/50 (P = 4.89e-27, k* = 7). Both clear their pre-registered thresholds. The FORCING half remains open - T, S, wind, atmospheric pCO2 and the DINN input channels still come from Darwin fields.

rows.question: Does CHL2_W_EXTRA improve Biggrow?
rows.answer: No, the pre-registered falsifier fired, the lever is DEAD. Ladder Biggrow: W=0 -> 6/50, W=8 -> 12/50, W=20 -> 7/50, non-monotone. W=20 also does real damage: scav_rat halves 26/50 -> 13/50, alpfe falls 49/50 -> 43/50, diatomgraz goes to 0/50. Smallgrow stayed flat at 5/50 across the whole ladder (the discriminating control held). STATUS must NOT be rewritten to say Biggrow responds to CHL2_W_EXTRA; the 12/50 at W=8 was a bump.

rows.question: Was the 'observable-set category error' real — were the identifiability profiles computed against total NPP, omitting silicate?
rows.answer: No, the premise is wrong in its specifics. (1) NPP was NEVER in the loss: `PRIMPROD_W` is unset in the 2026-07-07 config and defaults to 0.0 (`run_v3.0_joint_multi_aoi.py:458`, term gated at `:1734`). (2) A silica observable ALREADY was in the loss: `POSI_W=1.0` and `POSI_DARWIN_W=0.5` (`run_identifiability.sbatch:12-15`). The literal critique should not be repeated.

rows.question: Can more optimization (4000 epochs) bridge scav_rat and diatomgraz into a robust 4-of-4?
rows.answer: No, the trade-off is STRUCTURAL. At 4000 epochs: full+MLD gives alpfe 4/10, scav_rat 6/10, diatomgraz 0/10, R_PICPOC 10/10; pattern=0.3+MLD gives 10/10, 1/10, 0/10, 9/10. diatomgraz stays 0/10 in both, and adding MLD to the full-loss 4000ep run DEGRADES alpfe (49/50 -> 4/10) and scav_rat (41/50 -> 6/10). Job 192298, VERIFIED. This closes the 4-of-4 question.

rows.question: Does the depth emulator genuinely beat persistence on PIC/POC?
rows.answer: No, the win is MECHANICAL. Pooled skill vs persistence is +0.068 [-0.033, +0.143] (CI straddles 0) and vs the best free baseline -0.146 [-0.201, -0.099]. Against a free per-cell seasonal AR(1), PIC's edge vanishes (-0.037) and POC merely ties (+0.005). tend/anom ~0.9 makes persistence a weak straw man.

rows.question: Do surface and subsurface iron observations constrain the same parameters?
rows.answer: No, they invert cleanly. so_surf (surface iron): alpfe 49/50 RECOVERS, scav_rat 14/50. so_sub (subsurface iron): alpfe 14/50, scav_rat 33/50 RECOVERS. Surface identifies the SOURCE and cannot see the sink; subsurface identifies the SINK and cannot see the source. The combined fit (so_only, 30/50) is essentially the subsurface arm, and removing the surface term costs nothing (McNemar exact P = 0.69).

rows.question: Is the seismic checkerboard/spike test the same idea as the measured untrained null?
rows.answer: No, they sit on OPPOSITE sides of the control axis. Checkerboard is a POSITIVE control (known non-null input, full learning; catches 'the inversion cannot resolve this'). The measured untrained null is a NEGATIVE control (no learning at all; catches 'the score does not come from the inversion'). Shared virtue: both push something through the REAL pipeline rather than a linearised proxy.

rows.question: Does the FNO / neural-operator literature (GINO, Geo-FNO, PINO, AFNO, U-FNO, PhysicsNeMo, Earth2Studio) change the decision to shelve the parameter-conditioned calibration emulator?
rows.answer: No, unanimous verdict across 9 topics (8 reinforce shelving, 1 accelerates the UDE), keep it shelved. Blocker 1, data scarcity: GINO needed ~500 full CFD solves, U-FNO 4,500 ECLIPSE simulations of 5,500 total, FourCastNet ERA5 ~37 years hourly + ~1024 A100-GPU-hours; DarwinDiff has ONE v05 trajectory and no perturbed-Carroll-6 GCM ensemble. Blocker 2, dirty gradients: SC-FNO measured plain-FNO parameter-gradient R2 of only 0.21-0.82 despite accurate forward solutions (0.998 with sensitivity labels). PINO flips positive but argues FOR the UDE. Earth2Studio is an inference/coupling harness with no training, no autograd, no ocean/BGC model - do not add it to the Track-2 critical path. SCOPE NOTE (2026-07-11): 'shelved' covers ONLY the parameter-conditioned calibration emulator.

rows.question: Can an outsider re-derive the flagship n=50 headline from the checkout?
rows.answer: No. .gitignore:54 excludes runs/, and a repo-wide search for `per_aoi_recovered` returns ZERO JSON files. The 25/50 trio number and every per-AOI tally exist only in prose. This also blocks US from computing the same-AOI co-recovery number without pulling raw records off Explorer. Related: docs/findings/2026-07-23_emulator_multiseed.md, the sole source of the -0.161 headline, does not exist on the working branch (it lives on commit 6b10391) while STATUS.md:79 cites it.

rows.question: Will a fancier neural operator lift the emulator ceiling?
rows.answer: No. 14-agent adversarial scan of 7 Anandkumar-lab methods (918K tokens): GINO MEDIUM (conditional on a geometry artifact that was then disproved), CoDA-NO / SFNO / Markov-dissipative NO LOW, PINO / FunDPS / generative-score NO DEAD-END. The uniform verdict IS the answer: the bottleneck is data (~110 monthly pairs) and information (rank-1 inverse degeneracy, 1-step operator buys no horizon), not architecture. Publishable as a decisive negative.

rows.question: Does collecting more of the same observation type help the iron block?
rows.answer: No. A SECOND IDENTICAL surface [DFe] survey leaves the iron-block condition number UNCHANGED at 2930 and buys only the trivial sqrt(2) variance drop. What works is a different observable: a surface particulate-Fe scavenging-flux observable collapses it 2930 -> ~7, and subsurface [DFe] is nearly as strong because alpfe injects iron only at the surface. Organise the observation hierarchy by WHICH OBSERVABLE BREAKS WHICH DEGENERATE DIRECTION, not by data volume.

rows.question: Is the per-cell trio recovery a single-method DINN/autograd artifact?
rows.answer: No. A derivative-free EKI (J=256, 30 iters, wide log-uniform prior) run through the REAL geo1 box + real anchors reaches the same verdict as backprop: alpfe 0.999 vs Carroll 0.928 (rel.off 0.08, Cal-grade), R_PICPOC 0.036 vs 0.0425 (0.14, Cal-grade), scav_rat 2.1e-7 vs 6.0e-7 (0.65, Loose).

rows.question: Does collecting more of the same surface [DFe] data help the iron degeneracy?
rows.answer: No. A second identical surface-[DFe] survey gives exactly the trivial 2.00x variance drop, leaves the condition number unchanged at 2930, and has alignment 0.00 with the sloppy direction. POC, PIC and Fe-uptake flux behave the same (~2x, cond ~2170-2497).

rows.question: Does forward-reconstruction accuracy certify that an emulator is invertible for parameters?
rows.answer: No. A standard FNO reaches state R2 ~0.986 but only R2 ~0.21-0.82 on d(state)/d(parameter), and multi-parameter inversion collapses below R2 0.64; sensitivity-constrained training (SC-FNO, arXiv:2505.08740) restores >0.94. Crucially the sensitivity supervision uses FINITE DIFFERENCES, so it does not require a differentiable Darwin - (A)'s real cost is the PPE.

rows.question: Does the ocean-iron field use identifiability / sloppiness vocabulary for this degeneracy?
rows.answer: No. A targeted search across the FeMIP / SCOR WG151 / Tagliabue-Frants-Holzer-Pasquier-Somes lineage (including the SCOR WG151 final report and the Tagliabue 2017 Nature review) found NO paper using 'identifiability', 'sloppiness', 'equifinality', or 'parameter degeneracy' for the inter-model iron divergence - only domain language ('compensation between sources and sinks'). Naming it is therefore a genuine methodological contribution. Caveat: not-found-despite-search, not a provable true negative.

rows.question: Does adding prognostic SiO2 to the box fix diatomgraz identifiability?
rows.answer: No. Adding SiO2 is a DEFENSIBILITY win — it retires the M11 circularity objection and unlocks the ~630x GLODAP silicate data — but it is NOT a diatomgraz-identifiability fix. The growth-grazing ridge is the real obstacle and diatomgraz stays non-identifiable on real data.

rows.question: Does the depth-resolved emulator have real forecast skill?
rows.answer: No. Against a per-cell SEASONAL AR(1) baseline with 95% spatial block-bootstrap CIs the emulator is significantly WORSE than AR(1) at -0.146, and skill-vs-persistence is +0.068 [-0.033, +0.143], not significant. PIC/POC's apparent win was MECHANICAL (tendency ~ whole anomaly -> weak persistence denominator). Both 'beats persistence' and the v1 'beats climatology 5/6' claims are retired. (The four-seed -0.161 +/- 0.015, reproducing to -0.1614 +/- 0.0154 with ar1_seasonal_percell best in all 4 seeds, is a DIFFERENT artifact - see 2026-07-14_3d_emulator.md banner and evidence-matrix item 18.)

rows.question: Does the Track-2 depth emulator have real skill?
rows.answer: No. Against a per-cell SEASONAL AR(1) baseline with block-bootstrap CIs, the depth emulator's skill-vs-persistence CI straddles zero and it is WORSE than AR(1) (-0.16), robust across seeds 0-3 (job 188087). PIC/POC's 'win' was mechanical headroom. Retire 'beats persistence/climatology'. (Caveat: single AOI eqpac; a different AOI could differ, seed is ruled out.)

rows.question: Does chlorophyll beat persistence in the Track-2 emulator once log-space z-scoring is fixed?
rows.answer: No. All five Chl1 depth levels score NEGATIVE vs persistence: -0.47, -0.46, -0.48, -0.46, -0.61 (job 185256, B200, depth cube [48,25,171,360]). The log plumbing itself works — overall skill went from negative under linear z-scoring to +0.129 (verdict MAKE), carried by PIC/POC. Chl joins the persistence-dominated cluster (DIC -1.04, ALK -1.69, FeT -1.85), not the learnable one. Step (a) CLOSED.

rows.question: Is 'machine-checkable rather than human-filled' a defensible novelty axis for the identifiability contract?
rows.answer: No. Automated compliance checking of reporting standards has been mature ~7 years across four independent lineages: FAIR Evaluator / F-UJI / FAIRshake, SciScore, nf-core lint, and CONSORT-NLP -> AutoReporter -> RAPID plus the TRIPOD+AI tool. Even 'a missing item reads UNAVAILABLE rather than PASS' exists as `ignored` in nf-core lint and 'No information' in PROBAST - and PROBAST's is STRONGER, pushing the judgement toward high risk of bias rather than abstaining.

rows.question: Should the manuscript headline the 25/50 joint recovery count?
rows.answer: No. BINN was refereed down for leading with an aggregate metric (spatial r=0.86) that hid equifinality present even at 4 parameters. Lead with the per-parameter / per-combination identifiability verdict over the observable-4 instead.

rows.question: Is profile likelihood a practical identifiability tool for the sloppy iron pair (alpfe, scav_rat)?
rows.answer: No. Both profiles ran ~5x longer than R_PICPOC/diatomgraz (23 min) and were cancelled after >1:45 h with no verdict. Use the single-evaluation Gauss-Newton Fisher instead; it does not require the flat-direction re-optimization the profile chokes on.

rows.question: Is model capacity the bottleneck for the global-monthly emulator? Should we build a bigger model?
rows.answer: No. Capacity ladder (all seed 0): m48w96 +0.522, m64w96 +0.525, m64w128 +0.526, m32w128 +0.527 vs the m32w64 baseline +0.520 - only +0.007 for ~4x the parameters. Seed variance is +0.5165 +/- 0.0023 over 5 seeds, so the headline is not seed luck. But capacity saturation does NOT establish a ceiling: no ensemble control was run on this config, and the two configs where an 8-seed ensemble WAS run land BELOW +0.52. The doc's own wording: the ceiling claim here is UNSUPPORTED, not that a specific gain is proven.

rows.question: Would more capacity or more data extend the emulator's horizon?
rows.answer: No. Capacity: 4x params -> +0.007. Data volume: flat from n=55. Together with the bias result, the one-step error is at the floor for this architecture and dataset.

rows.question: Does R_PICPOC recovering 10/10 near 0.05 validate Carroll's 0.0425?
rows.answer: No. Carroll's own value is under-constrained, so the only honest statement is that the two are consistent within a wide band. Do not present it as a validation.

rows.question: Does the pre-existing daily emulator artifact (/scratch/qi_zim_neu/daily_v5/daily_train.json) settle the daily-emulator question?
rows.answer: No. Contaminated four ways: (1) the delta_t calendar bug is baked into its config (median_step_days 0.75, dt_hours 18.0 - it predates PR #186 by six days); (2) it was never scored against seasonal AR(1), the baseline that took the monthly ensemble from +0.48 to -0.161; (3) linear space, no --log-transform, on a field spanning ~2.8e6; (4) surfChl4 is numerically zero and was trained on anyway.

rows.question: Is a per-cell AR(1) baseline what kills the daily emulator (as it did the monthly one)?
rows.answer: No. Daily lag-1 r is 0.994-0.996 so AR(1) and persistence nearly coincide: AR(1) tendency-normalized error is 0.974/0.982/1.002/0.995 for surfChl1/2/3/5, at most 2.6% better than persistence. Overall skill vs persistence -4.0031 [-4.9470,-3.2036] vs AR(1) -4.0940 [-5.0561,-3.3212]; the baseline upgrade costs only 0.09. Log space is what kills it, not AR(1).

rows.question: Can daily ECCO-Darwin v5 output replace monthly for the parameter learner?
rows.answer: No. Daily v5 is surface-2D only — 16 diagnostics (CO2_flux, O2_flux, SIarea, SIheff, SSSanom, SST, apCO2, pCO2, pH, surfChl1-5, surfDIC_tend, surfPCO2, wspeed). It does not contain the 3-D tracers the loss uses (POC, PIC, DIC, ALK, FeT, subsurface DFe), which are monthly-only.
rows.doc: LOCAL-ONLY source, not in the repo: 2026-06-06_daily_data_defer.md

rows.question: Is alpfe an iron dust solubility?
rows.answer: No. Darwin3's own docs say to set it to 1 if the ironfile deposition is already soluble iron; ECCO-Darwin v05 forces with the soluble Mahowald-2009 product and sets ALPFE = 0.928. So alpfe is a near-unity dimensionless correction on already-soluble iron, not the ~1-2% fractional solubility of dust iron. The 'iron dust solubility' label was corrected in code.

rows.question: Is there an observational whole-ocean iron residence time to validate our recovered alpfe magnitude against?
rows.answer: No. Deep/whole-ocean estimates are regional and disagree by more than an order of magnitude: Hayes et al. 2018 give 6 +/- 3 yr for GA03 (integrated to 4 km); Bergquist & Boyle 2006 give 270 +/- 140 yr for NADW deepwater [secondary]. Only the UPPER ocean is constrained: Black et al. 2020 total-Fe 10-100 d for 67% of >100 estimates (median 33 d, range 1 d - 2.2 yr), dissolved-Fe ~20 d to 20 yr with most zonal means 1-4 yr; Croot 2004 6-62 d.

rows.question: Is the trio identifiability verdict an artifact of DINN + autograd (single-method attack)?
rows.answer: No. Derivative-free Ensemble Kalman Inversion (Iglesias-Law-Stuart 2013, J=256, 30 iters, job 189754, VERIFIED) reaches the same verdict: alpfe 0.999 vs Carroll 0.928 (rel 0.076, Cal-grade), R_PICPOC 0.0364 vs 0.0425 (0.143, Cal-grade), scav_rat 2.09e-7 vs 6.03e-7 (0.653, Loose, biased LOW in the same direction as the DINN fit). Report the posterior MEAN only - the ILS-2013 ensemble collapses, so its spread is not a calibrated posterior.

rows.question: Can a source-side (dust) anchor move scav_rat?
rows.answer: No. Dust-anchor A/B on B200 at n=10, both configs verify_run exit 0: scav_rat 0/10 in BOTH arms, medians 3.76e-7 (W=0) vs 3.75e-7 (+dust W=5) against Carroll 6.03e-7. The source anchor cannot move the sink leg; that needs a separate Phase-2 sink anchor (Cochran 210Po/210Pb + Black 234Th flux + the export partition), assimilating the FLUX not tau, presented as BOUNDING (~factor 2) not point-ID.

rows.question: Is the daily staging actually complete?
rows.answer: No. Expected 9860 records (iter 144 to 709992, stride 72). Actual .data files: surfChl1 9796, SST 9794, wspeed 9791 — each ~0.7% short, but MISSING DIFFERENT DAYS, so the 7-way intersection collapses to M=9392, losing 468 of 9860 (~4.7%). Same mechanism as the monthly mirror's 158-of-324. Changes nothing for Track 1; a bounded ~4% upside for Track 2 (re-score run already uses 6246 train / 2691 val pairs).

rows.question: Can any estimator (EnKF, CES/EKI, history matching, KOH GP emulator, SINDy) break the rank-1 alpfe<->scav_rat structural null?
rows.answer: No. Five independent routes in — EnKF rank <= N-1, CES flat ridge, history-matching NROY ray, KOH theta-delta ridge, SINDy non-uniqueness — all hit the same wall. No estimator breaks a rank-1 structural null. Adopt EKI/CES as a diagnostic only, never as a recovery improvement. (Note: this is about ESTIMATORS. New out-of-manifold OBSERVATIONS do break it — see the two-anchor OSSE row.)

rows.question: Is the alpfe/scav_rat degeneracy our discovery?
rows.answer: No. Frants et al. (2016) published the alpfe/scav_rat source-sink compensating family. Novelty must be repositioned to (a) the ECCO-Darwin-specific identifiability GEOMETRY and (b) the observation-design RESULT - and the observation-design work is a result on the surrogate, not a validated general method; drop the method claim.

rows.question: Is the alpfe/scav_rat anti-correlation just a local artifact of evaluating at Carroll's point?
rows.answer: No. GN-Fisher posterior corr is -0.773 at Carroll, -0.686 at seed-1 optimum and -0.686 at seed-2 optimum (2x2 condition numbers 2.2 / 4.9 / 4.9). Robust across >=3 points, consistent with Frants et al. (2016).

rows.question: Would adding prognostic dissolved SiO2 + Si-limitation to the 0-D box fix diatomgraz identifiability?
rows.answer: No. Given the biomass channel already in use, prognostic Si is at PARITY with the circular bSi diagnostic: rel_span 3.36 vs 3.31, well depth 0.0732 vs 0.0653, identical growth-grazing ridge (best-fit mu_d 0.55 -> 0.85). The gain is defensibility, not curvature.

rows.question: Is the v05-vs-MODIS r = 0.779 a skill number?
rows.answer: No. Growing-season only (May-Sep) r = 0.016, n = 80. The all-month r is carried by 'both fields have a spring bloom'. Any report of r = 0.78 must carry r = 0.016 alongside it.

rows.question: Does making the box's calcite source match Darwin's (COCCOLITH_ONLY=1) preserve R_PICPOC recovery?
rows.answer: No. In a matched local control pair (same seeds, same 2000 epochs, one lever) R_PICPOC per-AOI goes 10/10 -> 0/10 and the median lands at 1.012 = 23.9x Carroll. Per-AOI medians eqpac 1.067 / natl 0.999 / sopac 0.954 — uniform, not one bad basin, and not a bound artifact (PARAM_BOUNDS ceiling 1.5).

rows.question: Is the per-cell DINN win an artifact of per-cell absorbing physics the box omits outside eqpac?
rows.answer: No. In eqpac alone (the genuinely HNLC, iron-limited-year-round AOI) per-cell strictly beats global-scalar: scav_rat 7/50 vs 0/50 and R_PICPOC 46/50 vs 0/50. R_PICPOC's per-cell necessity is clean across all three AOIs.

rows.question: Does the >=2-of-3 'co-recovery' metric require the parameters to recover in the SAME AOI?
rows.answer: No. In scripts/analysis/grade_joint_percell.py:47-57 each trio parameter independently needs >=2 of 3 AOIs in band and the joint is the conjunction over parameters, with no requirement that the qualifying pairs overlap. The per-AOI tallies systematically differ: scav_rat's >=2 is carried by SO (49/50) plus eqpac (7/50) or natl (20/50); R_PICPOC's by eqpac (46/50) + natl (50/50) with SO weakest (40/50). A seed can count as a joint hit even if NO single AOI recovers all three parameters. One line in the grader fixes it.

rows.question: Does the two-anchor iron inversion point-identify alpfe and scav_rat on real data?
rows.answer: No. It breaks the rank-1 degeneracy in DIRECTION (lifts the ridge into a bounded basin) and bounds each parameter to a factor of a few: alpfe factor ~2-3 (the strong leg), scav_rat factor ~2 and combination-only. Honest posterior width is partition-dominated (~factor 2), not the ~1.4 that N~10 counting statistics suggest.

rows.question: Can the 21% Darwin-vs-B-SOSE iron offset be reported as a Darwin bias?
rows.answer: No. It can be reported as a model-model difference in total dissolved iron, but B-SOSE is a state estimate that assimilates observations, not truth. Establishing direction needs an observational anchor, not the second model.

rows.question: Does the calcite null depend on model-derived Omega?
rows.answer: No. It holds on fully independent in-situ carbonate data: recomputing Omega from GLODAPv3 bottle DIC/TAlk/T/S (NCEI 0315582, 2026; 838 eqpac + 1740 natl bottles), the per-basin exponents are non-significant - eqpac CI [-0.57, +3.02], natl CI [-8.32, +4.47], both spanning zero on <=0.17-dex within-basin support. The Omega solver itself is validated against PyCO2SYS at log-Omega r = 1.0000 on 2000 real points.

rows.question: Is Fe_TPL a clean scavenged-Fe proxy?
rows.answer: No. It includes biogenic cellular Fe (Fe_CELL, governed by growth/quota) and labile-lithogenic Fe (dust coatings scaling with deposition proportional to alpfe). This corrects an earlier claim in the same note.

rows.question: What is alpfe physically - is it an iron solubility?
rows.answer: No. It is a near-unity dimensionless scalar correction on an ALREADY-SOLUBLE iron flux. Darwin3's own doc says 'set it to 1 if the deposition rate in ironfile is already of soluble iron'; it is a single scalar multiply at darwin_forcing.F:483 with no dust->Fe conversion; v05 llc270 forces with llc270_Mahowald_2009_soluble_iron_dust.bin and sets ALPFE = 0.92831; Carroll 2020 Table 1 lists baseline 1 and GF optimum 0.9283; 0 of 20+ ecco_darwin configs use a total-dust product. Published fractional dust-Fe solubilities are <1-2% (Jickells 2005), ~3.1% global mean (Scanza 2018) - none is ~0.93.

rows.question: Is the Neural-BGC DOI 10.1029/2026GL123123 a fabrication?
rows.answer: No. It is a real, open-access GRL paper (received 24 Mar 2026, accepted 23 Jun 2026). The suspicious-looking '123123' article number and the initial 402-paywall on first access are both benign.

rows.question: Would probabilistic rollout or diffusion extend the emulator's horizon?
rows.answer: No. It is the WRONG prescription - it addresses chaos, which was measured absent (perturbation growth rate ~0, no positive Lyapunov exponent). This explicitly corrects an earlier draft of the same document that named it as the remaining candidate.

rows.question: Is the observations-only run actually independent of ECCO-Darwin?
rows.answer: No. It still uses use_darwin_ic=True and takes T, S, wind, atmospheric pCO2 and its DINN input channel from Darwin fields. 'Observations-only' currently means observations-only TARGETS, not end-to-end independence, and must be disclosed that way.

rows.question: Does scav_rat ever recover per-AOI in the n=10 covariate table?
rows.answer: No. It straddles in all 15 runs: cell-weighted reads 7/10 to 10/10 while honest per-AOI is 0-2/10, an inflation of +7 to +10 seeds. Quoting the joint scav_rat number overstates recovery in every arm.

rows.question: Does the diatomgraz 35/50 'non-circular handle via Chl+MLD' result survive?
rows.answer: No. Its architecture-matched untrained baseline (MLD_CHANNEL=1) is 34/50 = 0.68, so P(>=35 | p=0.68) = 0.447 - it beats an untrained network of the same architecture by a single seed. The separate geo1+MLD 10/10 result IS significant against the same baseline (0.68^10 = 0.021) but is far weaker than the alpfe / scav_rat / R_PICPOC results.

rows.question: Does adding the MLD channel to the FULL flagship loss give 4-of-4 per-AOI recovery?
rows.answer: No. Job 185779, n=10, 2000 epochs, rc=0, verify_run exit 0: alpfe 4/10, scav_rat 4/10, diatomgraz COLLAPSED to 0/10 (median 0.052 vs Carroll 0.83), R_PICPOC 10/10. At 4000 epochs (job 192298) diatomgraz is still 0/10 and MLD also degrades alpfe and scav_rat.

rows.question: Does improved Fisher conditioning convert into improved recovery?
rows.answer: No. Job 188077 showed subsurface [DFe] takes the {alpfe,scav_rat} GN-Fisher condition number from 3022 to 2.2 (~1400x), yet forcing the recovery loss to match that same profile harder makes recovery worse. Conditioning != recovery.

rows.question: Would conditioning the emulator on physical state (SST, MLD, wind, ice, shortwave) raise skill?
rows.answer: No. Joint R2 of the residual on 6 physical fields = 0.0136, permutation null 0.0053 +/- 0.0036, deltaR2 +0.0083, implied oracle bound on skill gain +0.0041. That best case is ~2.5x smaller than the harm already measured (-0.010 forcing concat, -0.073 seasonal encoding). The residual is not physics-shaped.

rows.question: Is the alpfe/scav_rat degeneracy an artifact of Darwin's ligand-free scavenging parameterization?
rows.answer: No. Lauderdale: the ocean iron cycle is 'open' because of its short residence time, so source and sink parameterizations really matter - the degeneracy is a property of the CYCLE, fundamental, not of our formulation. The ligand question is still testable but is not the explanation. His constructive response: 'This would be a good candidate for UDE!'

rows.question: Is the R_PICPOC 50/50 majority secretly a 2-AOI result?
rows.answer: No. Leg tally, measured on ctrl_n50 (the independent REPRODUCTION, not the published flagship): eqpac 47/50 (34 Daniels cells), natlsubpolar 50/50 (26 cells), southernoceanpac 40/50 (ZERO cells). Only 3 of 50 majorities REQUIRED the Southern Ocean leg, so the headline does not lean on it and the count is honest as a 3-AOI number. But the SO leg passing 40/50 with no anchor at all is itself the pooling signature. This section carries a SUPERSEDED banner: cite commit 57ee408's causal anchor-off control for the mechanism, not this correlational tally.

rows.question: Is 'diatomgraz-profile-with-MLD' a valid loss-landscape experiment?
rows.answer: No. MLD is a DINN INPUT channel; the profile evaluates L(theta) over a shared global theta[6] with training off, so an MLD profile would reproduce the MLD-off profile exactly. The MLD -> diatomgraz 10/10 result is a RECOVERY fact, not a LANDSCAPE fact.

rows.question: Do we need a Markov / dissipative neural operator for decadal UDE stability?
rows.answer: No. MNO targets state-norm blow-up under composition and there is no blow-up (finite=True, bounded drift to 100k steps). The Caltech scan's LOW rating is confirmed to dead-end with data.

rows.question: Is mirroring daily v5 to the laptop practical?
rows.answer: No. Measured throughput from data.nas.nasa.gov was ~100 KB/s (519 MB / ~100 daily records in 74 min, ~1% of the job). Extrapolated: ~4-5 days for SST alone, weeks-to-months for all 16 variables. Throughput is the blocker, not disk (full daily-2D ~800 GB fits in 1.5 TB free on D:). Pull it on the cluster instead.
rows.doc: LOCAL-ONLY source, not in the repo: 2026-06-06_daily_data_defer.md

rows.question: Is there any wired real rate-anchor for scav_rat in the learner?
rows.answer: No. No SCAV_ANCHOR_W loss term exists in scripts/run_v3.0_joint_multi_aoi.py. Of 12 observational loaders in src/darwindiff/, only three reach the flagship runner: geotraces_loader (:204), glodap_loader (:209, only if ALK_ABS_W>0), daniels_loader (:214). black2020_fe_flux_loader (234Th/sediment-trap Fe export flux, a real RATE) and xu_weber_loader have ZERO importers and no tests. cochran_gp15_po_pb_loader has 13 tests, all skipping on unstaged data. Wiring any rate anchor is a code task, not an env var. Grep for cochran/black2020/rufas2024 in the runner returns 0.

rows.question: Can an adjoint run supply the Jacobian the Gauss-Newton Fisher needs?
rows.answer: No. One adjoint integration returns J^T r — the gradient of a single scalar objective — not the observation x parameter Jacobian. For 4 controls, verified central differences are the correct route; v05 has no turnkey Darwin-controls adjoint.

rows.question: Can the v05 adjoint give us the Jacobian for a Gauss-Newton Fisher?
rows.answer: No. One adjoint integration returns J^T r, the gradient of ONE scalar objective, not the observation x parameter Jacobian a Gauss-Newton Fisher needs. For 4 controls, verified CENTRAL DIFFERENCES are the simpler route; v05 has no turnkey Darwin-controls adjoint. Use >=2 symmetric FD step sizes with identical checkpoints/forcing/averaging, and demonstrate convergence-with-integration-length.

rows.question: Is PARAM_LOG_SCALE defaulting to empty an undisclosed factor-of-five prior bug?
rows.answer: No. Only scav_rat is declared scale='log' (five of six parameters have no discrepancy at all), and both prior midpoints sit OUTSIDE the 0.40 Cal band - linear 1.515e-06 (rel 1.515), geometric 3.0e-07 (rel 0.502) - so no published count is contaminated. What must change is the wording plus prior_midpoint_offset(), which reports the geometric midpoint while training starts from the linear one.

rows.question: Does the docstring-prescribed pairing (COCCOLITH_ONLY + PIC_ABS_W > 0) rescue R_PICPOC?
rows.answer: No. PIC_ABS_W=0.02 pulls R_PICPOC from 1.012 to 0.149 (still 3.5x Carroll, recovery 1/10) and alpfe collapses 10/10 -> 1/10 (median 0.225), iron pair 0/10. There is no operating point in this screen where coccolith-only calcite and the trio coexist. The fix is not a weight.

rows.question: Can we claim to be first to frame ocean-BGC parameter recovery as sloppiness / identifiability?
rows.answer: No. Parameter identifiability in marine planktonic ecosystem models is a dedicated review field (10.5194/bg-14-1647-2017); AD for parameter inference is not new (AD Model Builder, 10.1080/10556788.2011.597854, 1750+ cites); the native inverse machinery exists (ECCO v4, 10.5194/gmd-8-3071-2015); the iron source/sink degeneracy is published (Frants 2016, 10.1002/2015JG003111) plus FeMIP; BGC observing-system design exists (BGC-Argo).

rows.question: Does adding prognostic silica to the box make diatomgraz identifiable?
rows.answer: No. Prototype shows prognostic-Si at PARITY with the circular bSi diagnostic (same growth-grazing compensation ridge); diatomgraz stays non-identifiable on real data (#152 open). It IS worth doing as a defensibility win: it retires the reviewer-M11 circularity criticism and unlocks ~630x more real data (~6,968 GLODAP silicate bottles vs 11 bSi).

rows.question: Is R_PICPOC's clean recovery an artifact of RATIO_MAX=2?
rows.answer: No. RATIO_MAX only clips the RATIO_W target, so with RATIO_W=0 it is a NO-OP in the flagship. main.tex l.1086 wrongly listed RATIO_MAX=2 as part of the geo1 config and has been corrected (it is the likely source of the red-team's #3 and #4). The genuine caveat is different: Daniels has zero Southern-Ocean coverage so the anchor auto-gates off there (n_daniels=0, l.1717); R_PICPOC is anchor-tested only in eqpac + natl.

rows.question: Does FourCastNet's ~45,000x speedup transfer to a BGC operator?
rows.answer: No. REJECTED as weather-specific (large tendency-to-anomaly ratio). Take the architecture, geometry and two-stage training recipe (pretrain one-step -> fine-tune on autoregressive rollout) only.

rows.question: Does our Track-2 forward emulator beat persistence at 1-month lead?
rows.answer: No. RETIRED. It does not beat a per-cell seasonal AR(1) baseline at 1-month lead, robustly across seeds. 'Beats persistence' must not be claimed anywhere.

rows.question: Do we need a NASA / NAS-HECC account to run ECCO-Darwin v05 ourselves?
rows.answer: No. Register a free Earthdata Login (15 min) instead. v05 is ALREADY BUILT on our own cluster: mitgcmuv binaries at /scratch/qi_zim_neu/darwindiff_v05/darwin3/build/ (767-rank, job 227366) and build468/ (468-rank, job 227523), with 49 GB / 140 files of inputs staged, 0 failures - both binaries confirmed on disk. The Darwin biogeochemical pickup is public with NO login (11.75 GB, data.nas.nasa.gov, timeStepNumber 78912 = 1096 days = an end-of-spin-up state near 1995-01-01, not a cold 1992 start). NAS/HECC eligibility needs a NASA grant/contract/WBS and the 2027 window closed 2026-07-20.

rows.question: Does a learned environment-driven calcite closure beat a constant (null) closure out-of-sample through prescribed transport — the pre-registered Track-2 make-or-break E2 gate?
rows.answer: No. Regularized closure (hidden 4, wd 0.01): learned R2 -0.05 vs null +0.50, delta -0.55. Default (hidden 16, wd 0): learned -1.53 vs null +0.50, delta -2.03. K_num ladder flat (-0.552 / -0.553 / -0.553), non-discriminating. A pass needed delta > 0 AND delta largest at physical kh; both runs fail both criteria. Replicated on a 10-seed H200 ensemble: the learned closure loses in every seed. Do not re-run this.

rows.question: Are the 13 committed silicate_scope Fisher/profile artifacts usable evidence?
rows.answer: No. Replaying all 13 through the new convergence guard rejects 9. Only Biggrow_nosi, Smallgrow_nosi, R_PICPOC_nosi and R_PICPOC_si survive, and R_PICPOC's span (~47) was never in question.

rows.question: Does the Southern Ocean have a real calcite anchor?
rows.answer: No. SO has no Daniels coverage; RATIO_MAX=2 is a sanitization workaround, not a constraint (without it low-POC cells inflate the target mean to 4.7e7 and collapse the loss). Do not trust SO in any calcite gate until a genuine SO PIC:POC anchor exists. Regional targets: eqpac 0.033 / natl 0.68 / SO 0.0067.

rows.question: Do Si observables alone identify diatomgraz?
rows.answer: No. Si-only (SiO2 + prognostic bSi, no biomass) puts the argmin nominally at truth (0.83 vs 0.830) but the well is ~16x shallower (0.0046 vs 0.0732), and the best-fit growth rate slides monotonically 0.60 -> 0.85 across the grid - the growth-grazing compensation ridge. The identifying power is carried by the biomass channel.

rows.question: Does the box's sign agreement with Darwin validate the Fisher transfer to the GCM?
rows.answer: No. Sign agreement is GUARANTEED BY CONSTRUCTION — carroll6.py reuses Darwin's own terms (alpfe*Phi_dust, scav_rat*DFe*POC, R_PICPOC*mort_total, diatomgraz*G0*P_large), so a source multiplier in Darwin is a source multiplier in the box. What is unvalidated is MAGNITUDE and CROSS-PARAMETER RANKING, and the Fisher eigenbasis (sloppy/stiff directions, EKI reparameterization) inherits exactly that ranking. The paper carries a verbatim scope caveat (doc section 6).

rows.question: Is there a continuous rank-deficient identifiability frontier as observation weights change?
rows.answer: No. Sweeping DANIELS_W in {0.5,1,4,8} x GEOTRACES_W in {1,3}, eqpac and natl stay rank 4/4 at EVERY weight. The softest observable direction does not rotate continuously - it stays alpfe-dominated (+/-0.93) except at down-weighted Daniels (danW=0.5) where it DISCRETELY flips to R_PICPOC. That is an optimizer/regularization effect, not an information frontier. Job 187731.

rows.question: Where do the three rain-ratio knobs live — one per file?
rows.answer: No. TWO are in `data.darwin` (`val_R_PICPOC` in &DARWIN_RANDOM_PARAMS, `a_R_PICPOC` in &DARWIN_TRAIT_PARAMS — `darwin_readparms.F:52-55` opens one file and passes the same unit number at `:66`); only &DARWIN_TRAITS comes from `data.traits`. A fourth knob `val_R_PICPOC_zoo` exists and is inert.

rows.question: Is the calcite identifiability limit specific to Omega as the driver?
rows.answer: No. Testing the other drivers Darwin plausibly keys on - SST and coccolithophore (Chl2) fraction - with a Simpson-robust within-biome (biome-demeaned) partial correlation, NO DRIVER clears the bar (significant AND sign-consistent within-biome). SST is well-excited within biomes (eqpac 4.8 C, natl 8.3 C, SO 9.7 C, unlike Omega's 0.08 dex) yet does no better: weak positive in eqpac (r ~ +0.4) and natl (~ +0.3) that the small SO sample (n=12) reverses. The limit is a property of the current climatological record. Only these three drivers were tested.

rows.question: Can the emulator negative be framed as a methodological contribution because the field baselines too weakly?
rows.answer: No. That fallback framing does not survive - at least one 2026 BGC emulator paper baselines correctly. We measured the same way and got a worse number (+0.055 +/- 0.013 vs persistence; -0.161 +/- 0.015 vs seasonal AR(1)).

rows.question: Can we convert Carroll-6 parameter identifiability into a quantified regional flux-error budget in Pg C/yr?
rows.answer: No. That requires a forward UOSSE that has not been run. The parameter->flux magnitude link is qualitative and a-priori only; this is flagged as the single easiest place in the positioning to overreach.

rows.question: Does the daily surface-chlorophyll emulator beat persistence?
rows.answer: No. The +0.408 headline is a linear-space number. Re-scored in log space on the same held-out set, three of four channels lose badly even on the strictly-positive subset: surfChl1 -1.71, surfChl2 -2.49, surfChl3 -12.43. Only surfChl5 survives (+0.1454). Verdict: the artifact does not support a daily MAKE.

rows.question: Are the v05 monthly time-mean targets progressively biased by the shrinking declared averaging window?
rows.answer: No. The .data are true full-month means. For iter 705672 (2017, declared window 10.5 d) rel-RMS vs the full-month mean is 1.53e-07 but 40.7 vs the declared-window mean; the 1992 control (iter 6552, declared 30.0 d) gives 3.09e-07 both ways. No published number is affected.

rows.question: Does the per-cell Fisher analysis need cross-cell coupling (KFAC)?
rows.answer: No. The 0-D box integrates every grid cell independently (no horizontal transport), so a per-cell parameter affects the loss only at its own cell and the field Fisher information is block-diagonal - a separate 6x6 per cell. The real-term sum reproduces the full aoi_loss to rel. err ~2e-8.

rows.question: Is a per-cell spatial CRLB map going to need KFAC or another large-matrix approximation?
rows.answer: No. The 0-D box is per-cell independent, so the field Fisher is block-diagonal (6x6 per cell); no KFAC needed.

rows.question: Does 'geo1 + MLD + DANIELS_RPICPOC_W=8 gives 10/10/10' contradict 'flagship-full + MLD gives diatomgraz 0/10'?
rows.answer: No. The 10/10/10 point is the ANCHORS-ONLY geo1 base (PINN_W=0, DUST_ANCHOR_W=0, pattern/chl/POC-sub stripped, job 178690 lineage); the 0/10 point is the reconstructed FULL flagship loss (job 185779). Two different operating points on the same 3-of-4 frontier; scav_rat is only ever recovered in the full-loss lineage.

rows.question: Is there a continuous identifiability frontier as anchor weights vary?
rows.answer: No. The 4-observable Fisher stays RANK 4/4 in eqpac and natl at ALL anchor weights; the softest direction DISCRETELY SWAPS (alpfe <-> R_PICPOC) with weighting, rather than rotating continuously. The Southern-Ocean rank-2 is fully explained by TWO missing anchors: R_PICPOC (no Daniels cells) plus diatomgraz (no bSi bins).

rows.question: Is the GHG Center's zonal-statistics / time-series path also broken?
rows.answer: No. The Raster API /statistics endpoint masks fill correctly (Coastal California: masked_pixels 245, valid_pixels 115, means near -6.7e-5), so the notebook time series is sound. The defect is confined to the STAC raster:bands metadata and anything derived from it (the notebook colorbar, off by a factor of 1.9e23).

rows.question: Does TPOSE distribute dissolved iron for an independent eqpac Fe-field comparison?
rows.answer: No. The actual directory listing at https://ecco.ucsd.edu/DATA/TPOSE/bgc_tp6/ (TPOSE.6-bgc, 2014-2016, monthly, domain 20S-20N) contains only CO2flux, DIC, O2, O2flux, SALT, SSH, THETA, UVEL, VVEL, WVEL, pCO2. No iron, and no nitrate/phosphate/alkalinity/chlorophyll either, despite all being named in the prose. Iron exists in N-BLING but obtaining it is an EMAIL REQUEST to the TPOSE group. TPOSE resolution is 1/3 deg nominal (not the 1/6 deg on Carroll's 2024 slide). The bgc_fwd run (2004-2019) is NOT assimilated and must not be used as external validation.

rows.question: Does the daily-cadence emulator beat a per-cell autoregressive baseline?
rows.answer: No. The daily version was off by about four in the wrong units; fixing the scaling recovers almost all of that, but it still loses to a per-cell autoregression. Daily autocorrelation is around 0.995, so that baseline is very hard to beat and more capacity is not expected to change it.

rows.question: Does using a paired rather than unpaired null change any headline?
rows.answer: No. The design is genuinely paired (identical initialisation per seed; Adam at lr=0 leaves weights bit-identical) but a zero baseline forces the discordant cell to zero, so McNemar collapses to 2^-k. alpfe 49/50, scav_rat 25/50 and 41/50, R_PICPOC 50/50 and trio 25/50 all stay decisive (weakest 2.98e-08); diatomgraz 35/50 stays not-above-chance (0.500 paired vs 0.447 reported).

rows.question: Does the 169× FeMIP iron residence-time spread need exotic physics to explain?
rows.answer: No. The identity τ = inventory / input reproduces every model's residence time exactly, so the 169× spread decomposes as 130× from input × 1.3× from inventory — a single source↔scavenging identifiability degeneracy. Tagliabue 2016 Table 2: τ 3.7 → 626 yr, concentration pinned at 0.58 ± 0.14 nM (~24%), total input flux ~140× (sediment source 0-194 Gmol/yr).

rows.question: Is the Track-2 emulator data-bound? Should we rebuild the cube for volume?
rows.answer: No. The learning curve is FLAT from n=55 (+0.4700 -> +0.4701 -> +0.4657), so more data is not the lever. The actual lever is Delta-t uniformity (+0.4730). The volume diagnosis was superseded the same day it was written.

rows.question: Is the Track-2 emulator data-bound — will more training pairs raise skill?
rows.answer: No. The learning curve saturates at n~55: +0.4167 (n=27), +0.4700 (n=55), +0.4701 (n=82), +0.4657 (n=110); 3 seeds per point at n=27/55/82 and 2 seeds at n=110; seed spread sigma 0.005-0.011. 55->82 buys +0.0001; 82->110 buys -0.0044.

rows.question: Is chlorophyll evaluated in ECCO-Darwin's own v05 evaluation white paper?
rows.answer: No. The official 135-figure white paper covers fCO2 / NO3 / PO4 / SiO2 / O2 / DIC / alkalinity against SOCAT / GLODAP / BGC-Argo, and no chlorophyll. This makes the comparison novel about THEIR model, but it is time-limited: v06 adds pkg/RadTrans, an ocean-colour forward operator.

rows.question: Should the E2 calcite rerun (pooled eqpac+natl, smaller/regularized closure) be run?
rows.answer: No. The oracle PREDICTS it will not recover identifiability: pooling two basins reaches only 0.25 dex (still below threshold) and a smaller closure cannot manufacture an Omega-dependence the data does not contain. The honest terminal result is the identifiability-limits write-up, not more GPU E2 runs. (The 2026-07-29 pooling finding makes this stronger: pooling ACROSS BASINS makes the confound worse.)

rows.question: Is the depth result in tension with the gauge-symmetry result?
rows.answer: No. The orbit is a symmetry of a SURFACE, SINGLE-LEVEL steady state; a second observation level is exactly the extra constraint that lifts it. No learned closure placed inside a multiplicative sink gains that information, which is why the UDE route stays closed while the depth route opens.

rows.question: Do you need to re-simulate 1992-2023 to run v05 perturbations?
rows.answer: No. The provided v5 pickup IS the assimilated state, so perturbation runs are short segments from it (1-3 yr) and are cheap. Run the control from the pickup first to confirm stability.

rows.question: Are the GHG Center's published raster:bands statistics for the ECCO-Darwin flux product correct?
rows.answer: No. The published mean 3.554192556042885e+19 and stddev 4.786401658343999e+19 are ENTIRELY the 1e20 land fill value counted as data: f = 186706/525312 = 0.355419 predicts both to ratio 1.000000. valid_percent reports 0.00019% (~one pixel) while the same block's histogram shows 338,606 non-fill pixels (64.46%).

rows.question: Do real, direct, Darwin-independent calcite observations constrain an Omega-driven rain-ratio closure?
rows.answer: No. The robust, defensible result is the NULL. Swapping the environment source from Marsh in-situ carbonate to the GLODAPv2.2016b OmegaC climatology FLIPS N.Atlantic bloom from +0.69 to -2.27 (p=0.98, n=59) and Patagonian from +0.86 to -1.07 (p=0.92, n=62); the two Omega sources agree only r=0.24 at the same cells; and point-level corr(log ratio, in-situ Omega) = 0.011. Consistent with Maranon et al. 2016.

rows.question: Does the 1-D column result (transport rescues held-out R2) mean transport rescues generalization on real data?
rows.answer: No. The synthetic 1-D column go/no-go is real but bounded: holding out ~30% of layers, a transport-free local box gives held-out R2 ~= -0.3 while the same fit WITH vertical mixing gives ~= +1.0. That is a SYNTHETIC VERTICAL-1D CAPACITY result, explicitly not the E2 gate. The real gate - held-out R2 > 0 on real GEOTRACES/calcite cells with HORIZONTAL transport - was later run and FAILED: learned R2 -0.05 against a null of +0.50, replicated across 10 seeds.

rows.question: Should we add wind / SSS / pCO2 / CO2-flux channels to the DINN input?
rows.answer: No. They DESTROY R_PICPOC: 6/10 -> 0/10, median blowing up to 0.216 (wind) and 0.380 (full) against Carroll's 0.0425. MLD alone does not do this (6/10 -> 5/10, median unchanged at 0.06). NOTE: this doc's recommended operating point 'geo1 + MLD only' is SUPERSEDED by geo1 + MLD + DANIELS_RPICPOC_W=8 (docs/findings/2026-07-23_rpicpoc_protection_result.md, STATUS.md:344), which restores R_PICPOC to 10/10; the wind/SSS/pCO2/CO2-flux prohibition itself is strengthened, since no anchor weight rescues R_PICPOC under wind.

rows.question: Does the flagship's scav_rat 25/50 contradict the July covariate runs' scav_rat 0-2/10?
rows.answer: No. They are different configurations. The July lineage deliberately zeroed DARWIN_PATTERN_W, POC_SUB_W, CHL1_W_EXTRA and NB23_PINN_WEIGHT, which the flagship carries. The manuscript is honest and internally consistent; do NOT report 'MLD costs scav_rat' as a clean causal claim.

rows.question: Do we need a custom torch.autograd.Function adjoint for the tridiagonal (Thomas) solver?
rows.answer: No. Thomas is a sequence of differentiable scalar ops; a pure-PyTorch loop over the Z axis (tens of layers) records ~2*Z ops and backprops exactly, with an O(Z) tape. torch.linalg has NO tridiagonal solver, so never route through the O(Z^3) dense solve, and do not reach for cuSPARSE/PCR (not autodiff-friendly; PCR only pays off at Z in the hundreds). The custom adjoint stays in reserve.

rows.question: Does the published reproducibility-appendix recipe reproduce the flagship?
rows.answer: No. Three load-bearing levers are absent: POSI_W=1.0, USE_EPPLEY_T=True, and per-AOI weights {eqpac 1, natl 2, sopac 2}. With the recipe as published, scav_rat and the trio are 0/10; adding only those three takes both to 8/10 (flagship n=50 is 25/50). Both runs verify_run.py exit 0.

rows.question: Can net primary production identify the growth pair {Smallgrow, Biggrow}?
rows.answer: No. Total NPP - the only real observable - gives only the biomass-weighted MEAN of mu_s and mu_l, so the pair stays a ridge. Per-PFT production would break it but is unmeasured; satellite NPP is Chl-derived and partly circular, only sparse 14C is independent. Growth is aggregate-observable-in-principle, not a positive E2.

rows.question: Does a production observable (NPP) rescue the growth pair Smallgrow/Biggrow?
rows.answer: No. Total NPP - what 14C and satellite actually measure - constrains only the BIOMASS-WEIGHTED MEAN growth rate, so the pair stays degenerate. In eqpac the large-phytoplankton rate is unidentifiable regardless (large phyto is negligible there) and total NPP adds nothing over biomass. Only a per-PFT production observable would split the pair, and no instrument measures it; the self-twin per-PFT 'pass' is the same construction tautology as the iron case.

rows.question: Does the Earthmover / Arraylake marketplace host ECCO-Darwin, ocean BGC, or satellite ocean-color data we need?
rows.answer: No. USEFUL-BUT-GATED (weak). Launch catalog was weather/atmosphere only; mid-2026 ocean additions are NOC and OGS physical hindcasts. No ECCO, no ECCO-Darwin, no MODIS/PACE/chlorophyll. The one adjacent asset is analysis-ready World Ocean Database (~90M profiles via Icechunk), convenience-only, already on our verified source list, behind a marketplace login that was not crossed.

rows.question: Does the flagship's calcification structure match Darwin's?
rows.answer: No. USE_COCCOLITH_ONLY_CALCITE = False (carroll6_5pft_2layer.py:158) and the flagship run record contains 'use_coccolith_only_calcite': false, so the box computes dPIC = R_PICPOC * mort_total with mort_total = mort_s + mort_l + graze_l (carroll6.py:225,231) - calcification from all FIVE PFTs - while Darwin applies the rain ratio to np = 2,3 only (v04, and types 2,3 in v05 data.traits) and to a per-group array in v06. The 50/50 R_PICPOC number stands but this belongs in limitations.

rows.question: Can a better estimator or architecture break the alpfe<->scav_rat degeneracy?
rows.answer: No. Verdict from an 11-agent literature pass: the degeneracy is breakable ONLY by a new observable that projects source and sink differently. No estimator/architecture change ever will, confirmed across 5 estimators + EKI. And every genuinely degeneracy-breaking observable needs a MODEL extension, because the binding blocker is that the Track-1 surrogate is a 0-D box that homogenizes away the vertical/section structure carrying the information.

rows.question: Do we need a new compute allocation, or Jon/NASA help, to run the 17-deck v05 GCM perturbation ensemble?
rows.answer: No. Verified live on Explorer 2026-07-25: `short` partition = 231 CPU nodes, 20+ cores each, 2-day limit, account c.schultz; Intel compilers/MPI/MKL + netcdf/HDF5 present; /scratch = 1.9 PB with 810 TB free; data.nas.nasa.gov llc_270 + iter42 inputs return HTTP 200 with no auth. Jon becomes an optional courtesy, not a compute favor. (Reinforced 2026-07-31: v05 binaries + 49 GB / 140 input files already built and staged on AICR /scratch.)

rows.question: Is vertical diffusivity kz the binding confound for the 1-D column iron fit?
rows.answer: No. With kz as a nuisance the CRLB stays 0.005. Remineralization is the binding confound: with kz + remin both floating the 4th Fisher eigenvalue is 0 and CRLB is inf (an EXACT null). Prescribing remin from v05 POC/POFe/primprod is therefore LOAD-BEARING, not optional.

rows.question: Does adding the Daniels calcite anchor disturb the iron pair?
rows.answer: No. Within the Daniels term all non-R_PICPOC parameters carry ~1e-11 to 1e-15 information (numerical zero) - only R_PICPOC lights up. The rain-ratio anchor is cleanly orthogonal to iron and growth.

rows.question: Does EDM diffusion add emulator skill?
rows.answer: No. Zero skill anywhere and -0.03 on 3-D (+0.421 -> +0.395) despite 2,048 forward passes per field against the deep ensemble's 8. It only wins calibration (0.375). Do not build diffusion for skill; ENSEMBLE.

rows.question: Are the emulator seasonal baselines correctly binned by calendar month?
rows.answer: No. _season_bin (scripts/analysis/emulator_baselines_v2.py:104-109) maps days to a month index by floor((t % 365.25) / 30.4375). Re-derived from disk: bin counts [23, 47, 24, 23, 25, 24, 23, 5, 36, 13, 40, 6] - Jan (21) + Feb (26) MERGED into one 47-member bin, bins 7 and 11 have 5 and 6 members, and Aug/Sep/Oct/Nov split across two bins. The published -0.161 +/- 0.015 AR(1) deficit is measured against a corrupted baseline. The error direction is CONSERVATIVE (correct binning makes the deficit larger), so the negative result survives but the number does not; by_init_month is invalidated outright.

rows.question: Can any profile likelihood of scav_rat computed against `ScavClosure` say anything about its identifiability?
rows.answer: No. `src/darwindiff/closures.py:130` gives the closure a FREE multiplicative level `self.log_r0 = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(math.log(base * self.POC0)))` (independently confirmed at that exact line), exactly redundant with `scav_rat`, so (scav_rat, r0) -> scav_rat*r0 is a one-dimensional exact redundancy and the profile is flat BY THEOREM rather than by measurement.

rows.question: Does a FLAT profile-likelihood span prove a parameter is non-identifiable?
rows.answer: No. alpfe is FLAT by the same diagnostic (nosi span 0.0235) and the project recovers it 9-10/10 (native-LLC270 eqpac, issue #110). Smallgrow (0.0050) and Biggrow (0.0049) are flatter still. This doc's wording: it is 'not supportable to present a FLAT span as evidence of structural non-identifiability without also explaining why the same diagnostic calls alpfe FLAT'. The word RETIRED for the diatomgraz headline is docs/research_notes/2026-07-23_manuscript_critical_path_plan.md, not this doc.

rows.question: Are the Po/Pb and Fe-export-flux sink anchors wired into the training loss?
rows.answer: No. cochran_gp15_po_pb_loader.py and black2020_fe_flux_loader.py both EXIST and are documented, but neither is wired into run_v3.0_joint_multi_aoi.py. Wiring them is E3, the highest-value experiment in the design document, because it is the only intervention predicted to move eqpac. It needs an observation operator (the box's scav_rat * DFe * POC removal term integrated to a flux), a variance entry, and the export partition pinned (rufas2024_poc_flux_loader) or the break does not happen.

rows.question: Does the emulator's 1-step error concentrate near coastlines or domain edges - i.e. would a geometry-aware operator (GINO / SFNO / CoDA-NO) help?
rows.answer: No. corr(err, coastal proximity) is ~0 in all four regions: natlsubpolar -0.033, npac -0.008, sopac +0.018, midatl -0.008. The error is SPATIALLY FLAT, so geometry operators drop from 'MEDIUM, test first' to dead-end-by-evidence for the regional emulators.

rows.question: Can the EKI ensemble spread be quoted as a posterior uncertainty on the Carroll-6 parameters?
rows.answer: No. eki_core.eki is the ILS-2013 inversion OPTIMIZER (no inflation/localization) and its ensemble collapses. The reported CVs (alpfe 2%, scav_rat 6.4%, R_PICPOC 3.6%) and the apparent alpfe<->scav_rat sloppy axis are NOT posterior widths; only the point estimates are load-bearing. A calibrated interval needs the EKS/sample stage (CES).

rows.question: Is the GEOTRACES profile-fidelity surface iron number trustworthy?
rows.answer: No. interp_to_axis (scripts/analysis/v05_geotraces_iron_profile_fidelity.py:107-123) uses np.interp, which clamps outside the data range, NaNs only the deep side, and leaves allow_shallow_clamp=True by default. Of 1053 qualifying stations, 538 have the 0 m value clamped upward from >10 m, 103 from >25 m, and 30 have BOTH 0 m and 50 m fabricated. Dissolved iron has a strong surface minimum so the clamp systematically INFLATES the value, and no clamp counter is emitted. Any 'v05 iron is Nx off at the surface' claim is unsafe until re-run with allow_shallow_clamp=False.

rows.question: Is the ~5x-low N-Atlantic chlorophyll bloom bias a coastal or discretization artifact?
rows.answer: No. natlsubpolar carries the highest error of the four regions (0.427 at dist 1-2, 0.406 at dist 2-5) but is flat in coastal proximity (corr -0.033). The bias is a bloom-dynamics/physics limit; the headline chl finding stands.

rows.question: Is our measured architecture-matched untrained baseline a methodological novelty?
rows.answer: No. novelty_survives: []. It is the MODEL PARAMETER RANDOMIZATION TEST of Adebayo et al. 2018 (NeurIPS 31, arXiv:1810.03292) - four of six hostile reviewers independently named it, one calling it 'the same construct, with the same justification, presented in the same register'. Antecedents: Oller et al. 2020 (arXiv:2004.07707), Schmidhuber/Hochreiter/Bengio 2001, Storrs et al. 2021 (10.1162/jocn_a_01755), Cadena et al. 2019, Combrisson & Jerbi 2015, and ocean data assimilation's free run.

rows.question: Does a particulate:dissolved iron partitioning observable (pFe/DFe) make scav_rat identifiable?
rows.answer: No. pFe/DFe reduces algebraically to scav_rat*POC/W_SINK (DFe cancels exactly), so the fit is tautological; the rate stays entangled with W_SINK/POC and a real contaminated Fe_TP re-injects the alpfe ridge. Not a realizable positive E2.

rows.question: Does scav_rat survive an anchors-only loss (all Darwin-pattern terms removed)?
rows.answer: No. scav_rat per-AOI collapses to 0/10 (from 25/50 in the flagship) while its cell-weighted count stays at 8/10 - the classic straddle. The joint trio also drops to 0/10 because scav_rat is the binding leg. scav_rat's per-AOI recovery is partially pattern-assisted, i.e. it leans on Darwin model output.

rows.question: Do covariate input channels rescue scav_rat?
rows.answer: No. scav_rat stays 0/10 across all five arms (the lone 2/10 at MLD+wind is within noise). The binding sink leg is unmoved by input information; it needs the Phase-2 sink anchor (234Th flux + export partition).

rows.question: Does the Southern Ocean local-identifiability result move the observable denominator off 4?
rows.answer: No. scav_rat was already in the denominator. What changes is the QUALIFIER: it is recoverable subject to a REGIONAL condition, and the flagship's 25/50 trio - whose sole binding leg is scav_rat - is carrying a basin-specific result reported as a global one.

rows.question: Does daily or seasonal data move the observable denominator from 4 to 6?
rows.answer: No. seasonal_chl_loss_batched (src/darwindiff/seasonal.py:122-134) needs chl_z of shape [12, 5, *spatial] and the only PFT-resolved chlorophyll that exists is Darwin's own (seasonal.py:74 says 'z-scored Darwin Chl targets'); MODIS-Aqua L3 gives one total field. PFT target = circular; bulk MODIS target = re-imposes the growth degeneracy. Separately, daily buys n_eff ~17-24 out of ~8,700 steps (lag-1 r 0.994-0.996, job 235995), fewer than the 158 monthly steps already held. The denominator stays at 4.

rows.question: Does ECCO-Darwin v05 have Omega/saturation-gated calcite dissolution?
rows.answer: No. v05 has NO disscSelect switch, constant-rate dissolution ONLY. The Omega-dependent Naviaux-2019 / Keir modes are a post-v05 darwin3 addition and do not exist in v05's code (verified at pinned commit 24885b71). Our two-layer box's constant R_PIC_DISSOL over 50-1000 m matches disscSelect=0 by construction. v05's exact Kdissc is unknown (~1/300 per day per ADR 0001:233); our default 0.05/day is ~15x faster.

rows.question: Does v05 have Omega-dependent calcite dissolution?
rows.answer: No. v05 has no `disscSelect` switch at all; the Omega-dependent modes are a later darwin3 addition, so v05 dissolves calcite at a constant rate by construction. Our own box does the same between 50 and 1000 m, and its default Kdissc looks roughly an order of magnitude fast. An Omega-null on the surface PRODUCTION ratio is what you would expect, not a data problem.

rows.question: Do v05 velocities need C-grid destaggering or rotation for the transport model?
rows.answer: No. v05 publishes velocities cell-centered and already geographic (`uVel_C` = UE_VEL_C eastward, `vVel_C` = VN_VEL_C northward), so `uVel_C` feeds transport zonal u DIRECTLY and must NOT be negated (a negation inverts the westward SEC). Validated: eqpac 12-month climatology surface u = -0.149 m/s (westward South Equatorial Current); div-free uniform-tracer tendency 6.25e-17. v05 land velocity is 0.0, not -999, so use `hFacC>0` to mask land. There is now a CI hermetic sign+unit test after a working-tree negation slipped in.

rows.question: Should we re-baseline the parameter learner to ECCO-Darwin v06?
rows.answer: No. v06 exists but is NOT released — Hong Zhang (JPL), ecco-support 2026-02-17: run 'Darwin v05 which is optimized/published', v06 'is still in optimization'. The only distributed product is still v5 (NASA GHG Center). Keep v05 as target, treat v06 as a monitored moving target.

rows.question: Is ECCO-Darwin v06 a valid replication target for the identifiability story?
rows.answer: No. v06 reformulates iron scavenging (SCAV_RAT rate → scav_tau + per-particle-class weights), makes growth/palatability/R_PICPOC group-specific with a different array layout, and adds a third iron source (hydrothermal vents) that could shift or break the alpfe/scav_rat degeneracy. A v06 rerun is not a replication without an explicit physical mapping. Validate on v05.

rows.question: What span threshold gates the iron/Monod branch of the symbolic-distillation oracle?
rows.answer: None — the Monod/iron branch distill() has NO span parameter. Its gates are inclusion ≥ 0.85, k stability ≤ 0.20, aliasing ≤ 0.95, held-out R² ≥ 0.90. The 0.30-dex figure everyone quotes is a distill_powerlaw default, i.e. the CALCITE branch. Pre-registering '≥ 0.30 dex' for DFe would green-light a support already shown to fail: narrow-regime seeds at 0.3107 / 0.3140 dex both DISTILL-FAIL on aliasing 0.9908 / 0.9904 despite held-out R² of 0.99999999. Aliasing cleared empirically near ~1.8 dex (1.819 / 1.837 dex, aliasing 0.805 / 0.813, 2/2 pass).

rows.question: Which Track-2 diffusion claims can be asserted?
rows.answer: None. All four (diffusion adds no skill -0.020/-0.026; diffusion improves calibration 0.375; the k1-vs-k8 horizon table; diverse-ensemble calibration 0.240) cite artifacts that are ABSENT (`diff_surf.json`, `diff_3d.json`, `diff_daily_eqpac.json`, `matched_k1/k8.json`, `opt_physics.json`). The whole generative-model line is currently unassertable.

rows.question: Where do we run NASA-side v05 perturbations now?
rows.answer: Not Pleiades — decommissioned 2026-01-07. Benchmark on Athena / Aitken / Electra, running one baseline + one perturbation first to size wall clock and I/O before budgeting all 17 runs (16 perturbed + 1 control, geometric steps x/1.1 and x/1.2).

rows.question: Does the alpfe sign-flip 'coin flip' claim replicate at n=50?
rows.answer: Not as symmetric. pattern loss 17/50 positive (0.34), Wilson [0.224, 0.478]; absolute loss 13/50 (0.26), Wilson [0.159, 0.396]. BOTH CIs exclude 0.5. But the equifinality claim SURVIVES: mean|r_alpfe| ~0.88 (excellent fit) yet both signs still occur across seeds. Required framing: 'init-dependent and not data-determined', NOT 'coin flip / symmetric double-well'.

rows.question: Was verify_run.py able to catch an unknown seventh parameter?
rows.answer: Not before PR #208. It hardcoded PARAMS and CARROLL, so a seventh parameter would have been trained, graded and written by the runner, SKIPPED by the gate, and the run would still have exited 0 VERIFIED. It is now registry-driven and rejects artifacts carrying parameters it does not know.

rows.question: Does up-weighting Chl2 (CHL2_W_EXTRA) recover Biggrow?
rows.answer: Not established. At n=50, Biggrow goes 6/50 -> 12/50 (Fisher p = 0.192, directional only) while Smallgrow is perfectly flat 7/50 -> 6/50 (p = 1.000) - the discriminating prediction P2 CONFIRMED. Biggrow at W=8 clears its untrained baseline (P = 3.1e-05) but the lever's arm-to-arm effect is not significant. Do not rewrite the STATUS 'unobservable by construction' claim yet.

rows.question: Does run-to-run nondeterminism flip any Cal grade?
rows.answer: Not in the sample measured: 0 observed flips of 60 (seed, param, AOI) units, grading two same-config replicates independently. 1 of 60 units had its own drift exceed its own margin - (seed 6, diatomgraz, eqpac), margin 0.0037 vs drift 0.0046 - and it did not flip. That parameter is already KNOWN_PRIOR_CONTAMINATED and not interpreted. No alpfe, scav_rat or R_PICPOC unit came within its own drift of the boundary. SCOPE: one pair, eqpac only, 10 seeds, N_STEPS=200, stripped loss - not the flagship.

rows.question: Is diatomgraz recovery circular (bSi back-solved from the model's own biomass)?
rows.answer: Not necessarily - it recovers 35/50 per-AOI at n=50 with POSI_W=0, through chlorophyll + MLD. The honest statement is 'recoverable from a non-circular but still model-internal observable, not recovered from independent real data'.

rows.question: Which parameters does the choice of collapse statistic actually affect?
rows.answer: ONLY scav_rat. alpfe and R_PICPOC are identical under arithmetic, geometric and median in every run measured, with per-cell log_sd <= 0.21 against the decisive threshold sqrt(2 ln 1.4) = 0.820; diatomgraz moves by at most one seed. The observations-only arms are exactly invariant (log_sd = 0.000). The collapse question is a scav_rat question and nothing else.

rows.question: Is the daily-cadence question open or closed?
rows.answer: OPEN for the emulator, CLOSED for the parameter learner (job 235995 plus the circularity result in 2026-07-30_daily_design_workflow_recovered.md). The pre-existing artifact does not move it either way.

rows.question: Which candidate improvements were killed before spending compute, and why?
rows.answer: Of 12 enumerated gaps: KILL as null-by-construction G7 (per-cell Fisher), G9 (cube-seam), G10 (UDE forcing as posed), G11 (field conservation as posed), G12 (discovery route-A); DEFER G5, G6; GO G1-G4, G8. The meta-finding is that the project's remaining 'gaps' are mostly identifiability LIMITS, not to-dos.

rows.question: What would it cost to actually settle the daily emulator question?
rows.answer: One modest Slurm job, NO retraining. scripts/analysis/emulator_baselines_v2.py already implements per-cell seasonal AR(1) with block-bootstrap CIs; it needs a predictions --fields npz the run did not save. Work: reload daily_emulator_eqpac.safetensors against the cube, dump predictions, re-score. Two caveats make it a new measurement: the cube was built pre-fix so the time axis must be rederived from `iters`, and surfChl4 must be dropped with scoring done in log space.

rows.question: Which covariate channels are safe to add to the DINN input, and which break R_PICPOC?
rows.answer: Only MLD is safe. Single-covariate matrix (diatomgraz / R_PICPOC per-AOI, n=10): MLD 10/10 / 5/10 (→10/10 at DAN=8); wind 10/10 / 0/10; SSS 7/10 / 0/10; pCO2atm 8/10 / 3/10; CO2-flux 10/10 / 0/10. Every carbonate/salinity-linked covariate breaks R_PICPOC and 8× anchor weight does NOT rescue wind (0/10, median pinned at 0.21 ≈ 5× Carroll at every anchor weight).

rows.question: Which Carroll-6 parameters can be perturbed by editing data.darwin?
rows.answer: Only `alpfe` and `scav_rat`. Exactly two of the four observables (R_PICPOC, diatomgraz) are trait-overridden and must be perturbed in `data.traits` (R_PICPOC types 2&3; PALAT diatom entries 36/43); the growth pair lives in PCMAX, also data.traits. alpfe/scav_rat are read by `darwin_read_params.F` and appear in neither the traits reader nor the generator. Proof it is live: the two v05 files already disagree (traits 0.0419 vs darwin 0.0425), so the 0.0425 recovery target is the generation scalar, not the loaded 0.0419.

rows.question: In which AOI does scav_rat actually recover in the observations-only arms?
rows.answer: Only southernoceanpac, in all three arms: obsonly_mld_litic 0/50 eqpac, 0/50 natl, 42/50 SO; obsonly_mld 0/50, 0/50, 39/50; obsonly_litic 0/50, 0/50, 50/50; untrained null 0/50. Whether that leg is local or inherited from the other basins is the open pre-registered question.

rows.question: Does the per-cell CRLB map prove the growth pair is unobservable?
rows.answer: Only the SPATIAL half. Growth-pair diagonal self-information is NOT negligible: full-loss info_sum Smallgrow ~1.8e-2 / 1.3e-2 / 1.0e-2 across eqpac/natl/SO, Biggrow ~6x smaller. What is confirmed is that the pair has no independent spatial footprint (it lights up only cells already covered by iron/Daniels/POSi). Unobservability is an OFF-DIAGONAL non-separability statement, not a diagonal one.

rows.question: What part of ECCO-Darwin does DarwinDiff actually touch?
rows.answer: Only the biogeochemistry source-minus-sink (SMS) kernel - the per-cell rate equations (darwin_forcing.F / gud_*.F upstream; carroll6_step / carroll6_carbonate_step in src/darwindiff/carroll6.py here) over 5-7 prognostic tracers. Circulation, mixing and nutrient-supply biogeography are baked into the v05 target fields and inherited as-is. The ~94% of other Darwin parameters stay at expert defaults, as Carroll left them.
rows.doc: LOCAL-ONLY source, not in the repo: 2026-05-21_jon_meeting_brief.md

rows.question: Which of the four observable parameters have an independent real anchor?
rows.answer: Only two. alpfe: YES, two of them (real surface GEOTRACES dFe + the Xu & Weber dust prior) - recovers 49/50 and method-independently. R_PICPOC: YES (real Daniels CP:PP), anchor-off collapses 50/50 -> 6/50 epoch-matched, but no Southern-Ocean Daniels coverage so it is anchored in 2 of 3 AOIs. scav_rat: NO independent real RATE observable is in the loss; recovery is model-pattern-assisted. diatomgraz: NO - the Chl target is Darwin's own output and POSi is a steady-state diagnostic. That 2-of-4 asymmetry, not the count 25/50, is the honest headline of the identifiability study.

rows.question: Is the alpfe/scav_rat pair strongly degenerate?
rows.answer: Only with SURFACE-ONLY iron. Surface-only (GEOTRACES_SUB_W=0): 2x2 condition 3022, conditional corr +0.999, sloppy direction co-varying (alpfe +0.64, scav_rat +0.77) = the S/k ratio. Surf+subsurface (what the real loss uses): condition 2.2, conditional corr -0.155, sloppy eigenvector alpfe-dominated (+0.98, -0.20). Subsurface [DFe] improves conditioning ~1400x (jobs 187666, 188077, both reproducible). The pair is LARGELY SEPARATED under the real data. Do not cite 'the strong -0.77 degeneracy' - that is the full-6 marginal, coupling-inflated.

rows.question: Is scav_rat anchor-driven or pattern-driven?
rows.answer: PARTLY SUPERSEDED — read both halves. On anchors alone scav_rat is 0/50 on the per-AOI >=2-of-3 metric, and its genuine majority recovery (25/50 at geo1, n=50) REQUIRES the DINN/per-cell spatial pattern loss; alpfe (50/50) and R_PICPOC (28/50) are by contrast ANCHOR-driven. But 'surface absolute anchors provably cannot do scav_rat' is REFUTED: with the Darwin-pattern term off, the southernoceanpac LEG recovers 42/50, 39/50 and 50/50 across the three observations-only arms against untrained 0/50, and a single-AOI southernoceanpac fit recovers 30/50 from GEOTRACES surface+subsurface iron alone (untrained 0.060, P=3.15e-24, verify_run exit 0). The 0/50 is an artifact of the 2-of-3 majority rule, not a measurement that nothing was learned. Local-vs-pooled for that leg is still unsettled (the anchor-off control that settled R_PICPOC has not been run for scav_rat).

rows.question: Does the geometric bounding map really cost R_PICPOC 5 seeds, as recorded on 2026-07-30?
rows.answer: PARTLY an arithmetic-collapse artifact. Job 264591 paired McNemar, linear vs geometric map: arithmetic 50/50 -> 45/50, 5 losses, P = 0.0625 (reproducing 227773); GEOMETRIC 50/50 -> 48/50, only 2 losses, P = 0.50; median 50/50 -> 47/50, 3 losses, P = 0.25. R_PICPOC is pooler-invariant in the FLAGSHIP configuration (log_sd <= 0.21), so this is not the scav_rat dispersion mechanism - it is that the two arms differ and grading the difference arithmetically overstates it. The surviving cost is 2 seeds, not 5. alpfe is 49/50 -> 50/50 under all three collapses, invariant as everywhere else.

rows.question: What was the pre-registered E2 calcite pass criterion, so we don't re-litigate it?
rows.answer: PASS <=> delta > 0 at physical kh AND K_num-shrinks (delta largest at physical kh, shrinking as kh grows over kh in {50,200,800}). Anything else is NOT a pass. Split: Omega_calcite upper quartile, hold='upper', q=0.25 fixed, n_val ~6 covered eqpac cells (train ~18) — acknowledged low-powered in advance. Metric: learned-minus-null held-out anomaly-R^2 vs the train basin mean, surface-gated closure. Config kh=50, kz=50, n_z=6, dt=0.25 d, dz=10 m. OUTCOME (separate doc): both runs failed both criteria.

rows.question: Why is the uniform-over-bounds null wrong for diatomgraz?
rows.answer: Parameters map through lo + (hi-lo)*sigmoid(theta) from a MID-BOUNDS start, and diatomgraz is the ONLY parameter whose initialization (0.525) falls inside its own Cal band [0.498, 1.162].
